Title: 'Very caring, soft-spoken': Yasin opens up on prison interactions with Najib
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Singer and composer Muhammad Yasin Sulaiman has recalled former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak as a gentleman during their time together at Kajang Prison.
Yasin said he got to know Najib while performing at prison events, where the former prime minister was often invited to dine with other guests.
He said he had never met Najib in person before being jailed.
"Thankfully, I had the opportunity to get to know him well because I was tasked with performing at every event," he said on the Dark Room Sessions (Sembang Seram) podcast.
The two would often share a table with the prison director and chat over their meals.
"When I met him in person, I found that he was a gentleman.
"He is very much a gentleman — very caring and soft-spoken," he said.
Yasin said Najib also took an interest in his case and asked about it several times.
"He asked about my case many times," he said.
Yasin said he had not expected the sentence handed down by the High Court, having believed he would be allowed to return home after a lower court discharged him.
"Suddenly, the judge handed down a sentence of 30 years and 16 strokes of the cane," he said.
The Petaling Jaya Sessions Court
acquitted and discharged
Yasin on three drug charges in November 2023, but ordered him to be placed at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta in Perak at the pleasure of the Sultan of Selangor.
The High Court subsequently overturned the acquittal in August 2024 and sentenced Yasin to life imprisonment and 16 strokes of the cane over the three drug offences.
However, the Court of Appeal in April 2025 allowed Yasin's appeal, acquitting and discharging him while maintaining the order that he be placed at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta.
Yasin was allowed to return home earlier this month after spending more than four years in prison and Hospital Bahagia.

Title: California takes aim at billionaires with proposed 5pct wealth tax
Article:
NEW YORK: No state may be a more natural fit for a tax on billionaires than California. The state leans left politically, needs funds for healthcare and is home to as many as 250 billionaires collectively worth upwards of US$2 trillion.
But the November 3 ballot initiative Proposition 40, which asks Californians whether to impose a one-time 5 per cent tax on the state's billionaires, is far from certain to pass, political analysts say, amid a debate that has raised questions about income inequality and the state's future business prospects.
Whether and how to tax the ultrawealthy are questions that extend well beyond the Hollywood Hills and Silicon Valley. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, a Democrat and democratic socialist, filmed a video in front of billionaire investor Ken Griffin's penthouse as part of an ultimately successful campaign to tax high-end second homes in the city. Even a majority of Republicans see billionaires as creating unfairness and contributing to economic woes, one 2025 poll showed.
A Reuters/Ipsos poll in August found 64 per cent of independent registered voters in the six-day nationwide poll said they support increasing taxes on corporations and billionaires, compared to 15 per cent who oppose the idea.
"Billionaires are no longer very popular," said University of California, Berkeley economics professor Emmanuel Saez, a researcher of wealth inequality who helped write Proposition 40. They have "enormous wealth, enormous power."
Saez describes the proposal as very simply "a tax on billionaires to fund healthcare."
California has more billionaires than any other state, according to a Forbes estimate last year, and is home to some of the country's most valuable companies, including tech giants Google, Apple, Meta and Nvidia .
POLLS SHOW IT AHEAD — FOR NOW
A UC Berkeley IGS Poll in August found 48 per cent of likely voters supported Proposition 40, with 41 per cent opposed, while a September Public Policy Institute of California poll showed it leading 52 per cent to 46 per cent.
California ballot measures typically need robust early support to survive Election Day. Undecided voters are more apt to vote "no" when the time comes, political analysts say, and opponents have yet to crank up their advertising campaign.
"California ballot measures tend to lose support over time, and if it's polling below 50 per cent in August, that's not a good sign for its prospects," said John Pitney, a professor of politics at Claremont McKenna College.
Backers say California's measure would generate US$100 billion for healthcare, food assistance and education. But skeptics peg the revenue estimate at closer to US$40 billion and say it could also drive some billionaires out of state, depriving California of future tax revenue and investment.
Opposition has been bolstered by billionaires such as Sergey Brin, the Google co-founder who has spent more than US$100 million to defeat Proposition 40 and support countermeasures on the same ballot that would effectively void it.
"I fled socialism with my family in 1979 and know the devastating, oppressive society it created in the Soviet Union. I don't want California to end up in the same place," Brin, 53, whose family left the Soviet Union when he was a child, told the New York Times.
Governor Gavin Newsom, a Democrat widely believed to be running for president in 2028, also opposes Proposition 40, instead advocating for a nationwide federal wealth tax.
COLORFUL INITIATIVE HISTORY
California ballot initiatives draw unusual attention because the state combines a powerful direct-democracy system with the nation's largest state economy and population. The process allows citizens to propose laws, though most initiatives are drafted by interest groups or lawyers.
Proposition 13 in 1978, which capped and rolled back property taxes, became a national symbol of a tax revolt that shaped US politics.
But California voters have only approved one in three citizen initiatives historically.
In 2022, another California ballot measure aimed at increasing taxes on top earners, Proposition 30, lost 58 per cent to 42 per cent, even though Democrats outnumber Republicans nearly two to one.
"Sixty percent of Californians now reliably vote Democratic for statewide races, but that doesn't mean that they're really liberal on taxing, spending, or even many social issues," said Thad Kousser, a professor of political science at UC San Diego.
European countries including France, Sweden, Finland, Denmark and Germany repealed wealth taxes between 1997 and 2018 amid concerns about capital flight, avoidance and economic competitiveness. The California proposition is retroactive to Jan 1, limiting billionaires' ability to escape the tax by moving.
Saez said the tax was unlikely to prompt many billionaires or the tech startups that are making people wealthy to move, because of the quality of California's universities, research, infrastructure and talent.
"It's just absurd to think that Silicon Valley is going to come to a standstill because of a billionaire wealth tax," he said.--REUTERS

Title: Sri Lanka sends monks skyward to summon rain amid severe drought
Article:
COLOMBO: Sri Lanka's Air Force said on Sunday it had flown Buddhist monks who prayed and sprinkled holy water over drought-hit areas in an attempt to encourage rain.
Sri Lanka's meteorology department has warned that both severe drought and heavy rains are likely to hit Sri Lanka during the rest of the year as the largely agricultural nation faces its "worst" El Nino climate phenomenon.
Three saffron-robed monks chanted prayers during Saturday evening's flight invoking the gods to end the drought, while airmen sprinkled holy water from five-litre plastic bottles.
An air force official told AFP the monks were flown aboard a Y-12 fixed-wing aircraft.
"As the nation faces the hardships of dry weather, the... aircraft takes to the skies in a symbolic act of compassion," the air force said in a social media post.
While the monks prayed for rain over drought-hit areas, the meteorology department has also warned of heavy downpours over other parts of the South Asian nation of 22 million people.
At Yala, Sri Lanka's largest wildlife park in the southeast, two out of six blocks have been closed to visitors because of the drought.
Weather experts have forecast that those dry conditions will give way to heavy rain from late September until December.
However, those rains are then expected to be followed by a prolonged drought early next year.
Water reservoirs, including those supplying hydroelectric power stations, are at around 50 per cent capacity, according to officials.
That compares well with previous years, but there are concerns if drought conditions intensify next year as forecast.
Sri Lanka's electricity utility has also held religious services in the past to appease the gods when hydro reservoirs run low.
El Nino is a natural climate variation that warms surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean, bringing worldwide changes in wind and rain patterns.
Human-caused climate change can amplify its effects because a warmer ocean and atmosphere make more energy and moisture available to feed extreme weather events.--AFP

Title: Man held after Chinese tourist allegedly assaulted in resort room
Article:
SEMPORNA: A man was arrested after a Chinese tourist alleged that someone entered her room and molested her at a resort in Jalan Kamiri here early yesterday.
Semporna district police chief Superintendent Tan Hiap Wah said the incident was believed to have occurred about 3am while the 25-year-old woman was sleeping in her room.
He said preliminary investigations found that the woman claimed she woke up after feeling someone removing some of her clothes before a struggle ensued when the suspect tried to grab her hand.
"The victim managed to escape from the room and hid in nearby bushes before she was found by a resort worker in the morning.
"While fleeing, the victim also claimed that the suspect pulled her hair, causing her to fall," he said in a statement today.
Tan said, acting on information and preliminary investigations, a team from the Semporna district police headquarters Criminal Investigation Division arrested the 18-year-old suspect about 8pm yesterday at the resort.
"The suspect was taken to the Semporna district police headquarters to assist in the investigation.
"The case is being investigated under Section 448 of the Penal Code for trespassing and Section 354 of the Penal Code for assaulting or using criminal force on a person with intent to outrage her modesty," he said.

Title: US warns Mideast war could 'escalate rapidly' after Riyadh missile attack
Article:
RIYADH: The United States warned that fighting between Saudi Arabia and Iran-backed Houthis could "escalate rapidly" after a missile attack targeted Riyadh for the first time since the Yemen conflict resumed.
US President Donald Trump cut short a weekend at Camp David, a secluded presidential complex in rural Maryland, to return unexpectedly to the White House on Saturday.
The White House gave no explanation for the early return, which comes as a new threshold was crossed in the conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, who control a large part of Yemen and are fighting government forces backed by a coalition led by Riyadh.
Loud explosions rang out on Saturday in the Saudi capital, where AFP journalists saw a fuel tank bearing the logo of oil giant Aramco on fire near the airport.
"This military conflict has the potential to escalate rapidly," the US State Department warned, adding American citizens outside the Middle East should "seriously reconsider travel to and through the region."
In recent weeks, the Houthis' lightning offensive seizing swathes of Yemeni territory has left hundreds dead and, according to the UN refugee agency, displaced more than 110,000 people.
- 'THWARTED'-
The violence has already disrupted exports from Saudi Arabia, the world's leading supplier of crude oil, as well as maritime traffic.
The United States, according to US news platform Axios, last week refused a Saudi request to strike the Houthis, but Washington has since approved a US$24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 fighter jets.
On Sunday, US Central Intelligence Agency Director John Ratcliffe met Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi in a rare visit to Cairo.
Sisi stressed "the paramount importance of settling regional crises through political and diplomatic tracks," according to a presidency statement.
The visit came days after Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman was also in the Egyptian capital, where he and Sisi urged safe and secure navigation through Bab al-Mandab, after the Houthis seized the Yemeni coast.
The Bab al-Mandab strait is a Red Sea waterway that is crucial to energy flows and global shipping and which has become even more strategic since Iran imposed a blockade on the Strait of Hormuz.
Condemning the Houthis' latest attacks, Turkiye's Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan told the broadcaster NTV that his country had had discussions with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, partners in a mutual defence pact, about possible assistance.
"In this regard, military needs, especially in state technical matters, may happen. There would be no problem in meeting this demand either," he said.
Saudi Arabia meanwhile has scrambled to contain the fallout of the Houthis' attacks on its territory.
On Sunday, the attack on Riyadh was not mentioned in several major Saudi papers, even though hours beforehand, the Riyadh-led coalition had confirmed that a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis was "successfully intercepted and destroyed."
The coalition added that the pro-Iranian fighters had tried to target "civilians and civilian infrastructure" in several cities in the west of the kingdom, including the port of Yanbu on the Red Sea, an important export hub for Saudi oil.
It said these attacks were thwarted by the Gulf monarchy's air defences.
Saudi Arabia has responded with scores of airstrikes on Houthi-held areas but has failed to stop the fighters' advance.
Claiming responsibility for the attack, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said fighters had carried out "two successful military operations using a large number of ballistic and cruise missiles and drones."
"The first targeted sensitive sites in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, and the second targeted Aramco facilities in Yanbu."
- LIGHTNING OFFENSIVE -
This is the first time since Yemen's civil war resumed that strikes have threatened the Saudi capital, piling further pressure on a global economy already rocked by seven months of war between the US and Iran.
Iran's top negotiator said Teheran had conveyed to the US through mediators its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, which it has blockaded throughout the Middle East war.
The Middle East war began in February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, which responded with retaliatory attacks on countries around the region.
Iran-backed groups also got involved, with Hizbollah in Lebanon and the Houthis in Yemen carrying out attacks against their foes.
While conflict in Yemen predates the Middle East war, the recent escalation in the country – one of the world's poorest – has turned it into the most active front of the wider violence.
A fragile truce reached in 2022 collapsed in July, and the Houthis went on an all-out offensive against the internationally recognised government this month.--AFP

Title: Iran tells US reopening Hormuz hinges on war ending, funds release
Article:
TEHERAN: Iran's top negotiator said Sunday that Teheran had conveyed to Washington through mediators its conditions for reopening the strategic Strait of Hormuz, which it has blockaded throughout the Middle East war.
The two foes are locked in a stalemate months into the conflict that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February.
Teheran has since maintained a stranglehold on the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping route for the world's oil and gas, while Washington is pushing a campaign to choke the Islamic republic's ports and economy.
"Our messages and the explanation of our conditions have been clearly conveyed to the other party through mediators," said Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who has acted as chief negotiator in talks to end the war.
"As long as the conditions are not met... and the US commitments are not honoured, it will be impossible to return to the situation from before the negotiations and to an open strait," he added, according to state television.
Mohsen Rezaei, the head of Iran's supreme national security council, said on Saturday that the Islamic republic had conveyed its conditions to the US via mediator Qatar.
"Our conditions are an end to the war on all fronts, the release of our frozen funds and an end to the naval blockade," he said in an interview with Al-Jazeera.
Iranian authorities have said that mediator Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi will travel to Teheran on Sunday for talks.
Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya central military command, meanwhile, issued a threat against the United States on Sunday, in a statement carried by state television.
"We warn that if the US makes a mistake in dealing with Islamic Iran, all of that country's bases and interests in the region will become the target of continuous, effective and painful attacks, without any limit or restraint," it said.--AFP

Title: KL, Labuan and nine states under thunderstorm, heavy rain warning
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain and strong wind warning for Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and nine states until 9pm today.
In a statement, MetMalaysia said the states involved are Perak, Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang, Selangor, Negri Sembilan, Johor, Sarawak and Sabah.
In Perak, the warning covers Hulu Perak, Selama, Larut Matang, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, Muallim, Bagan Datuk, Hilir Perak, Perak Tengah and Manjung.
It also covers Gua Musang, Kuala Krai, Jeli, Tanah Merah, Pasir Puteh and Machang in Kelantan.
In Selangor, the areas involved are Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor, Hulu Selangor, Gombak, Hulu Langat, Petaling and Klang.
The warning also covers Jelebu and Jempol in Negri Sembilan, as well as Mersing and Segamat in Johor.
In Sarawak, it covers Kuching, Serian, Samarahan, Sri Aman, Mukah (Mukah and Dalat), Bintulu (Tatau and Sebauh), Sibu, Kapit (Song, Belaga and Kapit), Limbang, Miri (Marudi and Beluru), Sarikei (Julau and Pakan), and Betong.
Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are also forecast in Kuala Pilah and Tampin in Negri Sembilan until 8pm.
In Sabah, the warning covers the Interior (Membakut, Beaufort, Sipitang, Tenom, Sook, Keningau, Tambunan and Kuala Penyu) and the West Coast (Papar and Penampang).– BERNAMA

Title: Tengku Zafrul: Childcare providers key to strengthening family economy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Childcare providers play a vital role in supporting the family economy by enabling parents to work while ensuring their children are properly cared for, said Prime Minister's Senior political adviser Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Tengku Abdul Aziz.
He said trusted childcare providers gave parents greater peace of mind while ensuring their children received proper care, making the sector an important part of the country's economic and social support ecosystem.
"We need to change the perception that it is merely a job. The reality is that the childcare profession is closely linked to parents' ability to work.
"Looking after those who care for our children is the same as looking after Malaysia's future," he said in his speech at the opening of the Central Zone Gala Pesona Kasih Madani at the Ampang Jaya Municipal Council convention centre in Taman Melawati today.
Tengku Zafrul said his interactions with communities had shown that families relied heavily on trusted childcare providers, particularly in enabling parents to continue working while ensuring their children's welfare.
He also said training, certification, recognition and legislation related to childcare should continue to be prioritised to strengthen professional standards and ensure the sector received due recognition.
In this regard, he said the views and challenges shared by childcare providers through the programme would be conveyed to the Finance Ministry and the Prime Minister for consideration in 2027 Budget planning, including support, training, certification and the expansion of related programmes.
About 600 informal childcare providers, family members, mentors, programme partners and stakeholders attended the Central Zone Gala Pesona Kasih Madani, which was organised to enhance the knowledge, skills and professionalism of home-based childcare providers in Malaysia.
Since its launch in August 2025, Kasih Madani has reached more than 1,000 childcare providers in Kuala Lumpur, Perak, Kedah and Penang through programmes such as the Madani Childcare Pilot Course (Karisma), Madani Childcare Seminar (Semai) and Madani Childcare Professionalisation Skills Mentoring (Bitara).
The initiative, implemented by Merdeka Centre with the support of Yayasan Sime Darby and the Finane  Ministry through 2026 Budget, also focuses on skills development, career planning, leadership, personal branding and mentoring to strengthen the professionalism of childcare providers.– BERNAMA

Title: [UPDATED] Preliminary report on Felda management due next week
Article:
SHAH ALAM: A preliminary report on the management of the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) is expected to be ready next week, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the government was spending RM980 million a year to cover Felda's losses.
"Next week, we will receive the preliminary report on Felda. 'Oh, this is revenge.' What revenge?
"I am responsible for Felda. Every year, we pay RM980 million to cover its losses," he said during his speech at the Perintis Reformis Reunion Hi-Tea here today.
Anwar dismissed suggestions of revenge or abuse of power, saying the judiciary remained independent in making its decisions.
"Can I speak to prosecutors or give my views to judges? No. Ask the Chief Justice. The Chief Justice has full independence and authority to decide," he said.
He said the government had taken responsibility for Felda's financial burden to ensure settlers did not have to bear the consequences of past losses.
Anwar also said he had approved RM450 million to repair Felda managers' homes nationwide after learning of their poor condition.
"Recently, I met Felda managers. Their homes were in poor condition and had not been repaired for 10 years.
"So I had to approve RM450 million to repair all Felda managers' homes nationwide," he said.
Anwar had previously said
issues involving a Felda subsidiary would be disclosed soon to identify weaknesses within the institution.
He said the disclosure was part of the unity government's efforts to address weaknesses and mistakes under previous administrations.

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar: Najib's pardon within his rights, other cases to proceed
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Datuk Seri Najib Razak's conditional pardon does not affect other legal proceedings against him, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar said every prisoner had the right to submit a pardon petition, with the decision ultimately resting with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
"We will continue with the cases still before the courts. The 1MDB case is continuing, and the civil cases are continuing," he said in his speech at the Perintis Reformis Reunion Hi-Tea here today.
Anwar said the advice he had given to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong on Najib's pardon petition did not point towards the decision that was made.
"The Pardons Board must make an assessment. There is advice from the prime minister and the Attorney-General, and ideally that advice should be heeded. However, the final decision rests with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
"Did my advice point towards that decision? No."
He said he had highlighted the ongoing cases, the size of the fine and the implications for public confidence in the system and international perceptions.
"I continued to remind them about the ongoing cases. I continued to remind them that the fine was too large.
"I also continued to remind them of the impact on public confidence in the system and the views of the international community. All these must be given consideration," he said.
Anwar said that while the prime minister's advice should be taken into account, he maintained that a pardon fell within the authority or discretion of state rulers or the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
"That is why, when the decision is made, we abide by it," he added.
Najib was granted a conditional pardon on Friday, allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine.
Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman also said the status of Najib's pending 1MDB court case
remained unchanged
despite the conditional pardon.

Title: Retired teacher hands over ATM cards, wife's gold necklace in RM15k scam
Article:
KOTA BHARU: A 75-year-old retired teacher in Bachok lost about RM15,000 after falling victim to a scam syndicate posing as police officers and handing over two ATM cards and his wife's gold necklace with a pendant.
Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said police arrested a 31-year-old woman in Kota Baru on Sept 13 to assist in the investigation.
He said the incident began on Sept 12 when the victim received a call from an individual claiming to be a police officer from the Johor contingent police Headquarters.
"The victim was informed that he had a court summons amounting to RM25,000 and was accused of involvement in money laundering and a drug syndicate, offences that carry a 15-year prison sentence.
"The call was then transferred to another individual claiming to be a senior police officer from Bukit Aman via WhatsApp," he said in a statement today.
Mohd Yusoff said the victim was instructed to keep the matter secret before being asked to surrender two ATM cards and his wife's gold necklace with a pendant, purportedly for an investigating officer who would come to his house.
He said that at 5pm on the same day, a woman arrived at the victim's house, collected the items and left.
"The gold necklace was subsequently sold at a gold shop in Kota Baru on the same day, while part of the proceeds was deposited into a third-party account.
"Based on preliminary statements, the suspect received instructions via WhatsApp from an unidentified individual to collect the victim's items," he said.
However, he noted that the victim managed to contact the bank to block the ATM cards and no transactions were detected.
He said police seized the victim's two ATM cards, a Perodua Axia, a bank-in receipt and a gold shop receipt, while the gold necklace was recovered from the gold shop.
"The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code," he said.
Mohd Yusoff advised the public not to panic or be deceived by threats of summonses and arrests, reminding them that the police, courts, Bank Negara Malaysia and banking institutions would never ask members of the public to surrender ATM cards, PIN numbers or jewellery.– BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar to meet Loke over resignation
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will meet Anthony Loke to discuss the latter's resignation from the Cabinet.
Anwar said Loke had informed him of the matter, but they had yet to discuss it further.
"He informed me, but I have not had the opportunity to discuss anything further. I need to hear his views.
"I understand because he is a principled person and has consistently opposed measures that could give the impression that we are weak or lenient towards corruption, especially when many others, including petty corruption offenders, face action.
"So, it is better that I meet him, hear his views and then make a decision," he told reporters after attending the Perintis Reformis Reunion Hi-Tea here.
Asked when he would meet Loke, Anwar said Loke might travel to Shanghai, China, first.
"Later, later. He is going to Shanghai, so perhaps he will go there first.
"I will be in Shanghai on Tuesday, after discussions with Premier Li Qiang," he said.
On possible Cabinet changes following Loke's resignation, Anwar said: "One thing at a time."
Yesterday, Loke announced his resignation as transport minister following the Federal Territories Pardons Board's decision to grant former prime minister
Datuk Seri Najib Razak a conditional house arrest
for his conviction in the SRC International case.
Loke announced his decision after a three-hour DAP central executive committee meeting to discuss the party's stance on the issue.
His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, on Friday, consented to a conditional pardon, allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine.

Title: Israel prevent over 100 Palestinian teachers from reaching schools in West Bank
Article:
RAMALLAH: The Israeli army has closed two checkpoints in the northern West Bank, preventing more than 100 Palestinian teachers from reaching schools, an education official said Sunday, Anadolu Ajansi reported.
Azmi Balawneh, director of education in Tubas Governorate, said 104 teachers were unable to reach their schools after the army shut the Tayasir and Ein Shibli checkpoints in the northern Jordan Valley, the official news agency WAFA reported.
He said the closures disrupted classes at six schools and a kindergarten attended by around 1,100 students.
The Israeli army closed the two checkpoints as part of broader military restrictions across the occupied West Bank.
Meanwhile, Israeli forces raided the village of Al-Mughayyir, east of Ramallah in the central West Bank, closed its main entrance and arrested dozens of Palestinians, according to local sources.
The sources told Anadolu that a large Israeli military force raided the village early Sunday, deployed across its neighbourhoods and searched Palestinian homes, supported by infantry units, military vehicles and a drone.
The closure of the village's main entrance disrupted school attendance and prevented workers and employees from reaching their workplaces, they added.
Al-Mughayyir has witnessed repeated Israeli raids and attacks amid escalating violence by Israeli settlers against Palestinians and their property in the area.
Since the start of Israel's war on the Gaza Strip in October 2023, the Israeli army and settlers have intensified attacks on Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.

Title: Najib faces continued legal battles despite house arrest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Although Datuk Seri Najib Razak has been allowed to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, his legal battles are far from over, including his appeal against a 15-year prison sentence in the 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) case.
The decision by the Federal Territories Pardons Board last Friday allows Najib to serve the remainder of his six-year sentence for the SRC International Sdn Bhd case under house arrest, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine and compliance with the conditions imposed.
However, the conditional pardon does not cover the separate 1MDB case.
On Dec 26, 2025, the Kuala Lumpur High Court convicted Najib on 25 charges of abuse of power and money laundering involving about RM2.3 billion in 1MDB funds and sentenced him to 15 years in prison and fined him RM11.4 billion.
Najib is appealing the conviction and sentence, with the 15-year sentence scheduled to begin after he completes his SRC International sentence.
A source said this had raised questions over what would happen if Najib's 1MDB appeal remained pending when his house arrest for the SRC International case ended in 2028.
The source said an appeal did not automatically stay the execution of a sentence. Instead, the defence would have to apply to the court for bail and a stay of execution, subject to the court's consideration.
"If the house arrest period ends in 2028, this means Najib would have completed his sentence for the SRC International case. However, he would still have other cases, including 1MDB, and his lawyers could apply to the court for bail and a stay of execution.
"Whether he could remain at home during that period would be determined by the court after the application is made. Otherwise, he would have to be detained in prison," the source said.
Najib, 73, was granted a conditional pardon by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong last Friday, allowing him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine and other conditions.
The Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister's Department said Najib must comply with all conditions imposed and failure to do so would result in the conditional pardon being revoked.
However, the division did not specify the conditions.
Najib was imprisoned in August 2022 after the Federal Court upheld his conviction for abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and money laundering involving RM42 million belonging to SRC International, a former 1MDB subsidiary.
He is serving a reduced six-year sentence at Kajang Prison after the Federal Territories Pardons Board halved his original 12-year sentence in February 2024.
His original RM210 million fine was also reduced to RM50 million.
In a separate civil case, the Kuala Lumpur High Court on March 31, 2026, found Najib liable for losses suffered by SRC International amounting to about US$1.3 billion.
The court found that Najib had breached his fiduciary duties, abused his position and misappropriated company funds for personal purposes.
The court allowed SRC International's claim for US$1.18 billion and ordered Najib to pay the amount, in addition to US$120 million he had previously received from the company, bringing the total to about US$1.3 billion.
SRC International filed the civil suit in May 2021, initially naming Najib and six former directors as defendants.
The company later dropped the six former directors from the suit, leaving Najib and former SRC International chief executive officer Nik Faisal Ariff Kamil as defendants.
A default judgment was entered against Nik Faisal in 2021, leaving Najib as the sole defendant in the proceedings.
Najib also faces other criminal and civil proceedings linked to SRC International and 1MDB.
On June 20, 2025, the High Court acquitted and discharged him of three money laundering charges involving RM27 million belonging to SRC International.
This followed the prosecution's failure to file its petitions of appeal within the stipulated period and to seek an extension of time to file them.
In another case involving six charges of criminal breach of trust over RM6.6 billion in payments to International Petroleum Investment Company (IPIC), Najib and former Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Mohd Irwan Serigar Abdullah were also acquitted and discharged.
Separately, 1MDB filed a civil suit seeking about US$5.64 billion from Najib and six others.
The trial before Judicial Commissioner Mohamad Redzuan Idrus is scheduled to resume on March 15 next year.
Najib is also facing a RM42 million civil suit filed by SRC International and its subsidiary Gandingan Mentari Sdn Bhd.
The case was concluded on March 16, and the parties are now making oral submissions before Justice Datuk Raja Ahmad Mohzanuddin Shah Raja Mohzan.
Meanwhile, the Court of Appeal on Sept 4 allowed a stay of bankruptcy proceedings against Najib and his son, Datuk Mohd Nazifuddin, pending the disposal of their appeals before the Special Commissioners of Income Tax concerning additional tax assessments issued by the Inland Revenue Board (IRB).
The bankruptcy proceedings stemmed from separate High Court decisions allowing IRB to enter summary judgments against Najib and Nazifuddin over unpaid tax arrears for the 2011 to 2017 assessment years.
IRB is seeking to recover RM1.69 billion from Najib and RM37.6 million from Nazifuddin.

Title: Caught red-handed: Man arrested after woman spots phone filming her in store toilet
Article:
JERANTUT: A 26-year-old woman realised she was being filmed on a mobile phone while using the women's toilet at a convenience store in Bandar Inderapura here yesterday.
The incident, which occurred about 10.30am, came to light after the woman, who was a customer at the store, noticed suspicious activity in the adjacent toilet.
Jerantut district police chief Superintendent Nor Azman Yusof said the victim, in her report, claimed she saw someone in the adjacent toilet filming her with a mobile phone over the top of the toilet partition.
He said the woman then acted quickly to check the adjacent toilet with the help of a family member.
"The victim's husband also contacted the Jerantut district police headquarters operations room for assistance.
"Personnel from the Jerantut police station's Motorcycle Patrol Unit (URB), who arrived at the scene, detained a 23-year-old man," he said in a statement today.
Nor Azman said police also seized an iPhone 16 Plus believed to have been used in the incident.
He said the suspect was remanded for 3 days until Sept 22 under Section 117 of the Criminal Procedure Code to assist investigations.
"The case is being investigated under Sections 509 and 377D of the Penal Code, while the seized phone will be sent to the police forensics division for analysis," he said.

Title: Man, woman found dead in car had previously planned to marry
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: A man and woman found dead in a car here early today had previously been close to getting married before ending their relationship, according to the woman's family.
The woman's 31-year-old brother said his sister had told the family that her relationship with the 34-year-old man had ended some time ago.
"They had known each other for a long time and were previously close to getting married, but it did not happen.
"My sister told me they had separated a long time ago, so I was shocked when a friend contacted me to say their bodies had been found together in the car," he said when met at the scene today.
The brother, who lives in Ampang, Selangor, said his sister was raised by their grandmother before moving in with their aunt in Kampung Pulau, Durian Tunggal.
He also identified his sister's body at the Alor Gajah Hospital Forensic Unit after being called by police to assist with the investigation.
Earlier, the bodies of a man and a woman were found by members of the public around 1am inside a car parked near a sewage treatment plant in Taman Inang Sari, Durian Tunggal.
Resident Shafie Manan, 71, said he became aware of the incident after waking at 3am to the sound of emergency vehicle sirens.
"When I opened the door, I noticed a foul smell. I asked a resident, who told me that the man, known as 'Pandan', had died inside the car with a woman," he said.
He said the man worked on a contract basis in road construction and lived with his family in the housing area.
Meanwhile, Beringin village secretary Muhammad Syamir Mohd Rozaman, 24, said several residents had earlier reported noticing an unusual smell in the area.
Alor Gajah police chief Superintendent Ahmad Abu Bakar confirmed the discovery and said post-mortem examinations were being conducted at the Alor Gajah Hospital Forensic Unit to determine the cause of death.
"The case is currently classified as sudden death. Further information, including the identities of the victims and cause of death, is still under investigation," he said.

Title: Leo XIV, first US pope transcends his restrained style
Article:
PRUDENT yet conciliatory, Pope Leo XIV has gradually imprinted his style on the leadership of the Catholic Church, finding his voice as he takes on some of the world's most pressing issues, from bloody conflicts to artificial intelligence.
When elected to lead the world's 1.4 billion Catholics on May 8, 2025, the former Robert Francis Prevost from Chicago had on-the-ground experience from more than two decades as a missionary in Peru, as well as insider knowledge of the Vatican and Roman Curia.
In the nearly year and a half since, Leo's character and priorities have more clearly emerged, revealing a pope unafraid to intercede in some of society's thorniest problems – whether trying to steer emerging technology in a more responsible direction, or exhorting leaders not to write off society's most disadvantaged.
After a recent spate of papal trips throughout Italy and abroad, including a visit to Africa in April and Spain in June, he will head to France next week, from Sept 25 through 28.
Leo has ancestors of Spanish, Italian, Quebecois, Monegasque and Creole extraction – as well as French, which the polyglot pontiff can read.
His paternal grandmother was born in France's western port city of Le Havre before emigrating to the United States at the start of the 20th century.
Soft-spoken, calm, and methodical, the pope who turned 71 this month has gradually revealed a more vocal side.
Martin Dumont, secretary-general of the Research Institute for the Study of Religions at the Sorbonne University in Paris, said that Leo XIV "wins people over."
"At first he seemed almost withdrawn, and eventually we saw the character reveal himself," Dumont told AFP.
Being American, "he very quickly managed to grasp the codes of modern communication, which wasn't necessarily the case with Francis," his Argentine predecessor, he added.
This year, he denounced corruption in speeches delivered in front of African leaders in power for decades, challenged Europe to receive, protect and integrate migrants, and defended himself against biting, personal attacks from US President Donald Trump.
Leo's interests – tennis, swimming, and his Chicago White Sox – go hand in hand with a relaxed relationship to the modern world: he wears a smartwatch under his cassock and has engaged with teenagers, mimicking the gestures of viral 6-7 trend.
But beyond style, the 267th pope is above all seeking to anchor his pontificate in the major transformations of contemporary society.
Leo's first encyclical, published in May, called for putting AI at the service of human dignity, a warning that has reverberated well beyond Catholic circles.
[[nid:1537000]]
"He's a scientist, a mathematician, someone who used to repair cars and computers. With the encyclical 'Magnifica Humanitas', he truly engages with the problems of our era, especially those linked to technology," Veronique Lecaros, author of "Leo XIV, Portrait of a Peruvian Pope," told AFP.
On the international stage, he has continued Francis's push for peace in ongoing conflicts, offering the Holy See as mediator between Moscow and Kyiv, while adopting a more forceful tone regarding the Russian invasion of its neighbour.
Moreover, Leo's opposition to Trump "helps make him popular", said Charles Mercier, director of studies at the Ecole Pratique des Hautes Etudes (EPHE) in Paris.
"It turns him into a figure of resistance to the danger of authoritarian populism," he said.
Born on Sept 14, 1955, the youngest of three brothers used to play priest, distributing candy discs as communion wafers to kids in his neighbourhood.
Ordained into the priesthood in 1982, he joined the mendicant Order of Saint Augustine, which he eventually headed in two consecutive terms from 2001 to 2013, a role that took him around the world visiting Augustine communities.
Sent as a missionary to Peru in 1985 – whose nationality he later adopted – he forged close ties with the local population over two decades-long missions.
He was later made the apostolic administrator of the Chiclayo diocese.
When he was made a cardinal by Francis in 2023, then-Archbishop Prevost was at the helm of the powerful Dicastery for Bishops, a key Vatican department that advises the pope on appointments.
In the Roman Curia, he built a reputation as a skillful mediator, acting as a bridge-builder between progressive and conservative voices.
Leo has been described as "the least American of Americans."
"I have great love for America," he said in a July interview with US broadcaster NBC.
But, he added, "I think of myself more as the pope who happens to be American."
* The writer is from AFP

Title: 27 areas nationwide record unhealthy API readings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Twenty-seven areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as at 4pm today.
Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) data showed that Sarawak had eight areas in the unhealthy range — IPD Serian (173), Samarahan (168), Sri Aman (157), Bintulu (155), Miri (153), Sibu (153), Limbang (116) and ILP Miri (106).
Serian was previously
placed under an emergency
after the King consented to its declaration following worsening haze.
Putrajaya recorded a reading of 161, followed by Nilai in Negri Sembilan at 160.
In Selangor, Shah Alam (157), Petaling Jaya (151), Banting (132), Kuala Selangor (108) and Klang (107) recorded unhealthy readings, while Batu Muda was the only area in Kuala Lumpur in the unhealthy range, at 147.
In Johor, Segamat (156), Batu Pahat (155), Tangkak (155) and Larkin (152) recorded unhealthy readings.
In Melaka, Bukit Rambai (153), Bandaraya Melaka (152) and Alor Gajah (119) also recorded unhealthy readings.

Title: PKR Youth dismisses calls for Parliament dissolution after Loke's offer to resign
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: PKR Youth has rejected calls to dissolve Parliament following Transport Minister Anthony Loke's offer to resign, stating that government stability is determined by the confidence of the majority in the Dewan Rakyat.
Its vice-chief Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari said calls by certain quarters for Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to dissolve Parliament did not reflect the current standing of the government.
"The stability of a government is determined by the mandate and confidence of the Dewan Rakyat majority, not by the sentiments or demands of state-level leaders. The unity government continues to hold that mandate.
"The dissolution of Parliament is a power provided under the Federal Constitution and should not be used as a tool for political pressure," he said in a statement today.
Earlier, Kedah Umno Strategic Communications Director Syed Mohd Johan Rizal issued a statement urging Anwar to dissolve Parliament after Loke offered his resignation in response to the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak.
However, Taufiq said the stance taken by the DAP secretary-general should be viewed as a leader acting responsibly rather than a sign of government collapse, with the final decision subject to acceptance by the prime minister.
The Youth and Sports Minister also dismissed claims that the Madani Government was "sinking", pointing to the country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth of 6.0 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, up from 5.4 per cent in the first quarter.
"A government that is 'sinking' could not possibly achieve such economic growth. This demonstrates the policy stability enjoyed by the public and highly regarded by investors," he said.
At the same time, the Sungai Petani MP said snap elections would only trigger uncertainty, derail ongoing programmes and strain national expenditure.
He noted that Umno was also part of the unity government, adding that Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had previously reiterated that the party would remain with the government until the end of its term.
"The people do not need an election triggered by political drama. What the public needs is a government that continues to work, an economy that continues to strengthen and living costs managed through proper policies," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Diana's brother compares media treatment of Harry, Meghan to late princess' ordeal
Article:
LONDON: The media's treatment of Prince Harry and his wife Meghan is on a par with that faced by his mother Diana, the late princess' brother said in an interview published on Sunday, warning that lessons needed to be learned from that period.
Diana died aged 36 in a 1997 Paris car crash as photographers pursued her on motorbikes, sparking an outpouring of grief and a reckoning over whether the media bore some responsibility for her death after splashing details of her life across front pages for years.
"If you look at an article in a tabloid about Diana or the couple that you were mentioning, Harry and Meghan, you know, they can be really, really unpleasant," Diana's brother, Earl Charles Spencer, told the BBC.
"And I think it would be really beholden on people to learn from Diana's example.
"I'm not here to speak for Harry and Meghan, but for anyone who's being destroyed in this way daily, it must be such a cancerous influence in their life."
Harry, Diana's youngest son, and Meghan, cited the impact of what they called a toxic media on their lives before they quit royal duties and moved to the United States in 2020.
They also sued much of the British tabloid press - with varying degrees of success - before they moved back to Britain in August.
Spencer has made headlines around the world in the last week after his book, "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister", was serialised in the Daily Mail, accusing her former husband, the now King Charles, of sounding "giddily elated" in the hours after her death.
The palace hit back by saying the king "is mindful that the pain of ​fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and colour ​memory in ⁠ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss."
The publication of the book and the return of Harry and Meghan to Britain are another challenge for the king, who is still undergoing treatment for cancer.
Diana's family accused the royals of showing a lack of support or care towards the late princess before her death, a charge that was repeated by Harry, who is now largely estranged from the rest of the royal family.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia rescue agency recovers another victim from capsized ship
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia's search and rescue agency said on Sunday it had recovered one more victim from the wreck of a passenger ship that capsized and sank in the Java Sea last weekend.
The passenger ship, Virgo Transport 8, was carrying 243 people, including 30 crew members, when it capsized in bad weather early on Sept 13 during a voyage from Surabaya in East Java to Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan.
"The victim was found by divers during a search inside the ship's hull," the agency said, adding that the victim will be airlifted out for identification.
The search and evacuation operation will be continued using divers and also air support, the agency said.
As of Saturday, authorities said nine people had been confirmed dead and more than 100 people had survived, leaving 126 unaccounted for.
The recovery operation for the sunken ship was extended by another week due to the number of missing people and because the salvage operation to right the ship is expected to take time, authorities said on Saturday.

Title: Najib house arrest decision first of its kind in Malaysia, says lawyer
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest is the first case of its kind in Malaysia, says a prominent lawyer.
Datuk N Sivananthan, the first Malaysian lawyer admitted to the International Criminal Court (ICC), said that in his experience, prisoners had previously been transferred from prison to alternative locations strictly on health grounds.
However, he said the current situation differs because the Pardons Board's decision specifically involves serving the remaining sentence under house arrest.
Sivananthan said the implementation of the decision raises key operational questions, particularly regarding the monitoring mechanism and who will oversee Najib throughout his house arrest.
"Similarly, questions remain on whether officers will be stationed at the residence, as well as the rules governing the entry and exit of visitors.
"All these matters must be determined based on directives and procedures to be established by the Prisons Department," he said.
The 64th Pardons Board Meeting for the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan, and Putrajaya convened at Istana Negara on Sept 18.
His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, who chaired the meeting, granted a conditional pardon allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine and other set conditions.
Commenting on the payment procedure, Sivananthan said the fine must be paid at the Kuala Lumpur High Court, as the original penalty was ordered by that court following Najib's conviction on seven charges of criminal breach of trust, abuse of position, and money laundering involving RM42 million from SRC International Sdn Bhd (SRC).
He said fine payments are typically made online via bank transfer to a court-designated account, eliminating the need for physical attendance at the Court Registry.
Once received, the bank verifies the transaction, and the receipt or proof of payment must be submitted to the court and the Prisons Department.
He added that no specific timeframe is fixed for the process, as it depends on payment processing and verification by the court.
"House arrest cannot commence until the fine is fully paid. Once the RM50 million sum is received and verified, the court will make the necessary arrangements and issue a receipt to be presented to the Prisons Department," he said.
From a legal standpoint, Sivananthan noted that Section 283 of the Criminal Procedure Code governs court authority regarding fine execution and payment procedures.
He said Najib must comply with the set fine conditions, as failure to do so would breach the conditional pardon terms, requiring him to serve out his sentence in prison.
Najib has been serving his sentence at Kajang Prison since Aug 23, 2022, following his conviction in the SRC International case.
On July 28, 2020, the Kuala Lumpur High Court sentenced him to 12 years' imprisonment and a RM210 million fine after finding him guilty on seven charges, a decision subsequently upheld on appeal.
Najib submitted a petition for pardon on Sept 2, 2022. In 2024, the Pardons Board reduced his prison sentence to six years and the fine to RM50 million, setting his release date for Aug 23, 2028, subject to set conditions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 15 motorcyclists arrested for reckless riding on Lekas
Article:
KAJANG: Police arrested 15 motorcyclists for reckless and dangerous riding during an operation targeting illegal street racing along the Kajang-Seremban Expressway (Lekas) early today.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said the five-hour Op Samseng Jalanan began at 12.01am.
He said police inspected 90 people and 70 motorcycles during the operation.
"A total of 15 motorcyclists were arrested under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for reckless and dangerous riding.
"Police also seized 34 motorcycles and issued 95 summonses for various traffic offences," he said in a statement today.
Naazron said a first conviction under Section 42(1) carried a jail term of up to 5 years and a fine of between RM5,000 and RM15,000.
"For a second or subsequent conviction, offenders face imprisonment of up to 10 years and a fine of between RM10,000 and RM20,000," he said.
Naazron said police would take action against anyone found riding or driving recklessly and endangering other road users.
"The public is advised to obey traffic laws and respect other road users," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: China's August oil imports from Russia rise as Middle East flows slump
Article:
BEIJING: China's crude oil imports from Russia stood at 11.2 million metric tons in August, or 2.64 million barrels per day (bpd), up 41 per cent from a year earlier and 23 per cent from July.
Imports from Malaysia, the largest transshipment hub for sanctioned Iranian oil, reached 2.6 million tons, or 620,000 bpd, down 45 per cent year on year but up 74 per cent from July.
Imports from Indonesia stood at 3.1 million tons, or 730,000 bpd, up 16 per cent year on year and flat with July.
China imported about 100,000 tons of crude from Indonesia in all of 2024, but monthly imports first exceeded 2 million tons in July 2025.
Reuters has previously reported that the surge in imports from Indonesia could reflect efforts to disguise shipments of sanctioned Iranian crude transshipped in waters off Malaysia.
Imports from Iraq stood at 1.4 million tons, down 75 per cent from a year earlier, while imports from Oman reached 900,000 tons, down 71 per cent year-on-year, after China recorded no shipments from the country in July.
Imports from the Saudi Arabia stood at 3.2 million tons, or 740,000 bpd, down 47 per cent year on year and down 41 per cent from July.
Imports from the United Arab Emirates stood at 2.9 million tons, or 680,000 bpd, down four per cent year on year but up 20 per cent from July.
Customs data showed no crude imports from the United States, Venezuela or Iran in August, in line with the prior year.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Najib touched by RM50mil fund support, says daughter [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: "Daddy really did not expect so many people to be willing to contribute," said Nooryana Najwa Najib, referring to efforts to raise money to
pay her father's RM50 million
fine.
The fundraising drive, organised through a 'Solidarity Fund', seeks to meet a condition of the conditional pardon granted to Datuk Seri Najib Razak, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
Nooryana said her father expressed how touched he was when she and her family visited the former prime minister at Kajang Prison yesterday.
She said he repeatedly expressed how touched he was to see people willing to contribute.
"Daddy really did not expect so many people to be willing to contribute," she said on Facebook today.
Nooryana, who is also Umno Puteri information chief, said her father had yet to be allowed to return home as the Pardons Board's decision stipulated that the RM50 million fine must first be paid.
She said the family respected the decision and that further arrangements would be made through official channels if they manage to raise the amount through the  Solidarity Fund set up by Umno.
"I understands that the fine must first be paid to the court. The court will then issue a receipt, which will be handed to the prison authorities.
"Only then can the prison authorities issue instructions for the house arrest," she said.
Nooryana said her family was also deeply touched by Umno's efforts to lead the Solidarity Fund and  that her father had never wanted to burden the party or the people.
Nooryana also expressed her appreciation to everyone who had asked about Najib and the family's well-being and prayed for their welfare.
"May Allah repay each of you for your prayers and kindness," she said.
Last Friday, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia granted Najib a conditional pardon to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to settlement of the RM50 million fine.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: National Welfare Foundation aid presented to family of late flight nurse Debra Moset
Article:
KUCHING: The National Welfare Foundation (YKN) has presented immediate disaster relief aid to the family of the late Debra Moset, a flight nurse who died in a Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, on Sept 8.
The aid was presented by Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri during a visit to the family's home in Kampung Semadang, Padawan, today.
Nancy, who is also the foundation's Board of Trustees chairman, said the assistance was a gesture of concern and support for the family following their sudden loss.
"This aid cannot replace a life lost, but I hope it helps ease the family's burden during this extremely difficult period.
"Peka YKN assistance is an early form of support for victims' families. In times like these, our presence and attention are important so that grieving families do not feel alone," she said.
The immediate relief aid was handed over to Debra's husband, John Then.
Also present were Puncak Borneo member of parliament Datuk Willie Mongin, YKN chief executive officer Nordina Haron and Women, Family and Community Development Ministry deputy secretary-general (Policy) Mohd Daud Mohd Arif.
Nancy said Debra's service and sacrifice in providing healthcare to rural communities would always be remembered.
She said Debra's mother, Renog Rasas, 71, would receive the Senior Citizens Assistance beginning next month, as well as the Kenyalang Gold Card and Senior Citizen Health Benefit.
Meanwhile, on Sept 18, Women, Family and Community Development Ministry secretary-general Datuk Dr Maziah Che Yusoff visited the family of the late Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin in Kampung Baung, Pengkalan Chepa, Kota Baru, Kelantan, to present PEKA YKN assistance.
Similar assistance has also been arranged for the families of three other crash victims — the late Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham in Senawang, Negri Sembilan, and the late Alexson Adit Henry and Jessie Paya Jok in Miri.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sungai Gurun breaches danger level, flash floods hit 2 villages
Article:
YAN: Sungai Gurun in Kampung Perupok here breached the danger level following more than two hours of heavy rain today.
According to the Department of Irrigation and Drainage's (JPS) Infobanjir website, the river's water level had risen to 4.43m, exceeding the danger level of 3.5m.
The rise in water levels caused flash floods in Kampung Teroi Bukit and Kampung Titi Teras following the overflow of the river.
Yan Civil Defence District Officer Lieutenant (PA) Zul Izzi Zulkifli said 11 houses in Kampung Teroi Bukit and eight in Kampung Titi Teras had been affected by floodwaters so far.
He said no temporary evacuation centre (PPS) had been opened in the areas as of now.
"Residents are advised to remain alert to the flood early warning system," he said when contacted today.
Zul Izzi also advised residents to be prepared to evacuate if the river's water level continued to rise.
He said his personnel were currently monitoring several areas in the district at risk of flooding.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trial begins for 14 men in Kelantan cross-dressing case [WATCH]
Article:
KOTA BARU: The trial of 14 men accused of wearing women's clothing and acting like women began here today, with an enforcement officer taking the stand.
Lawyer Muhammad Syarafi Mohd Salleh said four enforcement officers involved in the operation were expected to testify.
"The prosecution started presenting its case today, and one witness was called.
"We were informed that four enforcement officers are expected to testify," he told reporters after the proceedings.
Syarafi said his clients had cooperated throughout the case and were later released on RM1,000 bail each with one surety.
Earlier, Lower Syariah Court judge Wan Firdaus Wan Ibrahim set Jan 24 next year for the trial to resume, allowing both sides to complete several outstanding documents.
The 14 men were charged at the same court in December last year with wearing women's clothing and shoes and acting like women at the multipurpose hall of Troika Residency, Jalan Sultan Ibrahim, at 11pm on May 30, 2025.
They pleaded not guilty and were charged under Section 19(1) of the Syariah Criminal Code (I) Enactment 2019, which covers the offence of men acting like women.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: North Korea fires ballistic missile off east coast, Seoul says
Article:
SEOUL: North Korea launched a ballistic missile off its eastern coast on Sunday, its second test in roughly a week and days after Pyongyang accused the US of driving tensions on the Korean Peninsula through a series of military drills.
South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said it detected the test firing from the Wonsan area around 3pm (0600 GMT), identifying the weapon as a ballistic missile.
Japan's defence ministry also said it appeared to be a ballistic missile.
Japanese public broadcaster NHK said the projectile had come down outside Japan's exclusive economic zone.
South Korea's National Security Council condemned the short-range missile launch, which follows a test on Sept 12.
The council urged Pyongyang to immediately cease missile activity, warning that the test directly violated UN Security Council resolutions.
On Saturday, North Korea dismissed a resolution by the UN nuclear watchdog against Pyongyang's nuclear programme.
Pyongyang last week also condemned a US-led naval drill which included South Korea and Japan and which ran from Aug 29 to Sept 10 near Guam.
North Korea's Kim Yo Jong, the influential sister of leader Kim Jong Un, on Friday blamed US-led military drills for "ever-worsening" tensions on the Korean Peninsula and vowed no change in the country's course to strengthen its nuclear arsenal.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hotspots, peat fires and palm oil: Why tracing Malaysia’s haze is so complicated
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 20 — The return of the haze across parts of Malaysia has once again brought forest and land fires in the region into focus.
But as smoke spreads and satellite images light up with hotspots, the question of where the fires are and what caused them is not as straightforward as it may appear.
Malaysia’s response this time includes an offer of firefighting assistance to Indonesia, which reflects the fact that the haze does not stop at national borders.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi on Thursday said Malaysia had offered a Bombardier CL-415MP aircraft, three helicopters and 52 officers and personnel from the National Disaster Management Agency, Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) and the Royal Malaysian Air Force.
The offer was conveyed to Indonesian vice-president Gibran Rakabuming Raka during his four-day working visit to Indonesia. It will be referred to President Prabowo Subianto for approval.
The CL-415MP, operated by MMEA, is capable of aerial firefighting. It was previously deployed to South Sumatra in 2015, when it dropped 546,000 litres of water during a five-day operation.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also the National Disaster Management Committee chairman, said the offer to assist was to help Indonesia tackle transboundary haze, rather than interfering in its affairs.
The urgency is clear from the air quality readings in Malaysia.
As at 5pm on Friday, 32 areas recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System portal, Johan Setia in Selangor recorded the highest reading at 183, followed by Shah Alam (169), Petaling Jaya (162), Banting (161) and Klang (159).
Sarawak recorded the highest number of affected areas, with Kuching recording an API reading of 174, followed by Samarahan (167), IPD Serian (166), Sibu (162), Bintulu (161), Sarikei (155), Sri Aman (154) and Kapit (153).
Putrajaya recorded an unhealthy reading of 172, while Batu Muda and Cheras recorded 167 and 165, respectively. Temerloh and Jerantut in Pahang recorded 155 and 151.
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality; 51 to 100, moderate; 101 to 200, unhealthy; 201 to 300, very unhealthy; and 301 and above, hazardous.
For the public, the immediate concern is the smoke. For those trying to trace the fires, however, the picture is more complicated.
Indonesia was reported as saying that it was complying with Asean’s existing haze response mechanisms, including daily reporting of hotspot data, projected smoke movements and firefighting measures.
Asean activated a Level 3 alert for severe transboundary haze on August 26. Under the mechanism, member states share information to help neighbouring countries take precautionary measures.
At the same time, the haze has once again revived questions about the role of the palm oil industry in regional fires.
The Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB), however, said regional forest and peat fires could not be attributed primarily to oil-palm cultivation, with satellite mapping currently showing hotspots across multiple land uses.
These, it said, include unmanaged areas, pulpwood plantations and small-scale farming plots.
Director-General (DG) Datuk Badrul Hisham Mohd said human land-clearing activities remained a major driver of fires, while severe climate anomalies such as El Niño could amplify their spread.
“From a scientific standpoint, El Niño and prolonged dry weather act strictly as environmental amplifiers, not the spark itself,” he told Bernama.
That distinction matters when looking at the fires.
Badrul Hisham said wildfires did not occur spontaneously in the region’s humid climate, with ignition generally associated with human activity.
Prolonged dry weather, however, reduces soil and vegetation moisture, allowing fires to spread more rapidly.
The problem becomes harder to manage in peat areas, where drained peat can dry out and burn below the surface.
Badrul Hisham said this can make fires difficult to detect and extinguish.
“Once ignited, peat fires can continue smouldering underground and may reignite even after surface fires appear to have been brought under control.
“The resulting emissions can continue for weeks or months and, depending on wind direction, contribute to prolonged transboundary haze,” he said.
When fire risk rises
The newly-appointed DG also stressed that the Malaysian oil palm industry should not be described as having a seasonal open-burning practice because zero burning has already been established within the industry through the mandatory Malaysian Sustainable Palm Oil (MSPO) Certification Scheme, enforced since January 2020.
It is the risk of fire that changes with the seasons, he said.
That risk generally increases during prolonged dry periods, particularly from June to September during the southwest monsoon, while some regions also experience a dry window around January and February.
Lower rainfall, declining soil and peat moisture and higher temperatures during these periods make accidental or unauthorised ignition more likely to spread, with El Niño capable of further intensifying the risk.
There is also a need to be careful when reading satellite hotspot maps.
A hotspot is an indicator of possible fire. It is not, by itself, proof of open burning or evidence of someone starting a fire.
“That distinction matters, because a hotspot can identify where a fire may be occurring, but not necessarily who started it, or what land use is involved.
“For Malaysia and Indonesia, therefore, the immediate challenge is twofold: containing the fires and improving the ability to identify their causes,” he said.
For now, Malaysia’s offer of aircraft, helicopters and personnel is focused on putting out fires.
But the wider haze problem is unlikely to be solved by firefighting alone.
Prevention, land management and early detection remain part of the equation, as does cooperation between countries sharing the same airspace and, at times, the same smoke.
The palm oil debate will continue, particularly whenever the haze returns.
Therefore, satellite hotspots alone cannot settle that debate. Fires occur across different types of land, and weather conditions can determine how quickly they spread and how long they persist.
That makes identifying the actual source and cause of each fire just as important as putting it out.
For Malaysia, Indonesia and the wider region, that may be the more difficult part of dealing with the haze. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Najib has right to seek pardon, but wider impact must be considered
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has defended former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s right to seek a pardon, while cautioning that its impact on public confidence and international perceptions must also be weighed.
Anwar also rejected suggestions that he had paved the way for Najib’s conditional pardon, saying every prisoner had the right to submit an appeal for consideration.
“When people say that I was the one who paved the way [for that pardon], that is not true.
“What I said is that every prisoner has the right to submit an appeal, and I stand by defending that right for anyone, including Datuk Seri Najib.
“He has the right to submit his appeal for consideration by the Pardons Board, which is chaired by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, and the board must consider it,” Anwar said at the Hi-Tea Reunion Perintis Reformis event in Shah Alam today.
He said the prime minister and attorney general could provide advice on the matter, while the power to grant a pardon rested with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
Anwar added that he had continued to remind the Pardons Board that Najib’s ongoing court cases, the size of the fine and the potential impact on public confidence and international perceptions should not be overlooked.
“I continue to remind [the board] about the ongoing cases.
“I continue to remind them that the fine is exceptionally large.
“I continue to remind them that its impact on public confidence in the system, as well as international perceptions, must be given serious attention,” he said.
The Federal Territories Pardons Board granted Najib a conditional pardon on Friday, allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine and other conditions.
Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar has clarified that the conditional pardon applies only to the prison sentence imposed in the SRC International case.

Title: Anwar to meet Loke before deciding on resignation, says no letter submitted yet
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he will meet Transport Minister Anthony Loke to hear his views before deciding whether to accept his resignation.
Anwar said Loke had informed him of his intention to step down following the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak but had yet to submit a formal resignation letter.
Speaking to media in Shah Alam today, Anwar said he wanted to sit down with Loke before making any decision.
“I have to listen to his views, and I understand because he is a principled person.
“From the very beginning, he has been consistent in opposing measures that could give the impression that we are weak or lenient towards corrupt practices — especially when action is taken against many others, including those involved in petty corruption.
“Therefore, it is best that I meet him and hear his perspective,” Anwar said.
Anwar said Loke had informed him of the decision after chairing an emergency DAP central executive committee (CEC) meeting yesterday, but told him he would bring the resignation letter when they met to discuss the matter.
“He [Loke] held a meeting yesterday and informed me about it. He said he would bring the letter when we meet to discuss the matter.
“I told him, ‘It’s fine, whenever we have the time.’
“After this, I will be heading to Melaka. Tomorrow, he will be leaving for Shanghai, while I will be going to Shanghai on Tuesday for a meeting with Premier Li Qiang,” he said.
Asked about the possibility of a Cabinet dissolution, Anwar said the government was taking matters “one by one” for now.
Loke, who is also DAP secretary-general, announced yesterday that he had offered to resign as transport minister following a nearly three-hour emergency CEC meeting at the party’s headquarters in Pudu.
He said he would submit his resignation letter to Anwar soon, while remaining DAP secretary-general and Seremban MP. Other DAP ministers and deputy ministers will remain in the government.

Title: Childcare is economic infrastructure, not ‘just a job’, says Tengku Zafrul
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — The childcare profession should be regarded as an important component in supporting the family economy and not merely as a job involving the care of children, said the Prime Minister’s Senior Political Adviser Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Tengku Abdul Aziz.
He said having trusted childcare providers enabled parents to work with greater peace of mind while ensuring that their children received proper care, making the childcare sector part of the country’s economic and social support ecosystem.
“We need to change the perception that it is merely a job. The reality is that the childcare profession is closely linked to parents’ ability to work.
“Looking after those who care for our children is the same as looking after Malaysia’s future,” he said in his speech at the opening of the Central Zone Gala Pesona Kasih Madani at the Ampang Jaya Municipal Council Convention Centre, Taman Melawati, here today.
Tengku Zafrul said his experience interacting with communities had also shown how families relied heavily on trusted childcare providers, particularly to enable parents to continue working while ensuring their children’s welfare was taken care of.
He also said that training, certification, recognition and legislation relating to childcare should continue to be prioritised to ensure that the profession had stronger standards and received due recognition.
In this regard, he said the views and challenges shared by childcare providers through the programme would be brought to the Finance Ministry and the prime minister for consideration in the Budget 2027 planning, including aspects of support, training, certification and the expansion of related programmes.
About 600 informal childcare providers, family members, mentors, programme partners and stakeholders attended the Central Zone Gala Pesona Kasih Madani, which was organised to strengthen the knowledge, skills and level of professionalism of home-based childcare providers in Malaysia.
Since its launch in August 2025, Kasih Madani has reached more than 1,000 childcare providers in four states — Kuala Lumpur, Perak, Kedah and Penang — through programmes such as the Madani Childcare Pilot Course (KARISMA), Madani Childcare Seminar (SEMAI) and Madani Childcare Professionalisation Skills Mentoring (BITARA).
The initiative, implemented by Merdeka Center with the support of Yayasan Sime Darby and the Ministry of Finance through Budget 2026, also focuses on skills development, career planning, leadership, personal branding and mentoring to strengthen the professionalism of childcare providers. — Bernama

Title: Fake cops scare retired Bachok teacher into handing over ATM cards and wife’s gold necklace
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 20 — A 75-year-old retired teacher in Bachok lost about RM15,000 after being duped by a scam syndicate posing as police officers, which also resulted in the victim handing over two ATM cards and his wife’s gold necklace with a pendant.
Kelantan Police Chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said that the police arrested a 31-year-old woman on September 13 around Kota Bharu to assist with the investigation of the case.
He said the incident began on September 12 when the victim received a phone call from an individual claiming to be a police officer from the Johor Contingent Police Headquarters (IPK).
