“The victim was informed that he had a court summons amounting to RM25,000 and was accused of being involved in money laundering and a drug syndicate, which carries a 15-year prison sentence.
“The call was then transferred to another individual claiming to be a senior Bukit Aman police officer via WhatsApp,” he said in a statement today.
Mohd Yusoff said the victim was then instructed to keep the matter secret from anyone before being asked to surrender two ATM cards and his wife’s gold necklace with a pendant, purportedly to be handed over to an investigating officer who would come to his house.
He mentioned that at about 5:00 pm on the same day, a woman arrived in a car at the victim’s house, collected the items, and left.
“The gold necklace was subsequently sold at a gold shop in Kota Bharu on the same day, while a portion of the proceeds from the sale was deposited into a third-party account.
“Based on preliminary statements, the suspect received instructions via WhatsApp from an unidentified individual to collect the victim’s items,” he said.
However, he noted that the victim managed to contact the bank to block the ATM cards, and no transactions were detected.
According to him, the police seized the victim’s two ATM cards, a Perodua Axia car, a bank-in receipt, and a gold shop receipt, while the gold necklace was successfully recovered from the respective gold shop.
“The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code,” he said.
Mohd Yusoff advised the public not to panic or be deceived by threats of summonses and arrests, reminding them that the police, courts, Bank Negara Malaysia, and banking institutions will never contact members of the public to ask them to surrender ATM cards, PIN numbers, or jewellery to any party. — Bernama

Title: Haze tightens its grip: 32 areas now recording unhealthy API readings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — Thirty-two areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4.30pm today, according to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal.
The highest reading was recorded at Serian IPD, Sarawak, at 173, followed by nine other areas in the state which also recorded unhealthy API levels — Samarahan (168), Kuching (166), Sri Aman (157), Bintulu (155), Miri and Sibu (153 each), Samalaju (131), Limbang (116) and ILP Miri (106).
Other areas with unhealthy API readings included Putrajaya (161), Nilai, Negeri Sembilan (160), Shah Alam, Selangor (157), Seremban, Negeri Sembilan (156), and three areas in Johor - Segamat (156), Batu Pahat and Tangkak (155 each).
Kota Kinabalu Polytechnic in Sabah recorded an API reading of 155, followed by Cheras in Kuala Lumpur and Bukit Rambai in Melaka (153 each), Melaka City and Larkin in Johor (152 each), and Petaling Jaya in Selangor (151).
Other affected areas were Batu Muda, Kuala Lumpur (147), Banting, Selangor (132), Port Dickson, Negeri Sembilan (126), Alor Gajah, Melaka (119), Indera Mahkota Kuantan, Pahang (111), Kuala Selangor (108), Klang (107) and Balok Baru Kuantan in Pahang (103).
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and 301 and above hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Cop’s knock wakes startled Audi driver before wrong-way scare in Johor Bahru
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 20 — A video posted on social media showing a car being driven against traffic on Jalan Jim Quee here has been traced to an Audi driver who is believed to have fallen asleep after finishing work.
The incident took place at about 6.50am on September 18 and involves a Malaysian man who works as a restaurant waiter at R&F Mall, South Johor Bahru district deputy police chief Superintendent Ng Swie Chait said in a Facebook statement today.
According to Ng, the man was driving an Audi home to Taman Mount Austin after finishing his shift that day.
Upon arriving at the Tanjung Puteri traffic-light intersection, he fell asleep inside the vehicle.
A police officer nearby saw that the car was not moving and approaching, knocked on the window to get the driver’s attention.
The knock woke the driver, Ng related, adding that the former then slowly moved the car forward into traffic.
But possibly disoriented, the Audi driver was travelling against the flow of traffic towards Jalan Jim Quee.
Officers nearby then tested the driver for alcohol consumption, using an SD2+ breathalyser, which came back negative.
Ng said the case is being investigated under Section 79(2) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for disobeying traffic signals.

Title: Police: Foreign man who caused disturbance at KLIA suspected of having mental health issues
Article:
SEPANG, Sept 20 — A Bangladeshi man who behaved aggressively and disturbed passengers at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1 on Thursday is suspected of having mental health issues.
KLIA district police chief ACP M. Ravi said the man had shouted loudly and disturbed passengers at an airline counter at KLIA Terminal 1 at 4.40pm.
“Terminal security personnel who arrived to bring the situation under control took the suspect to the Terminal 1 police station for further action.
“During the cooling-off period, the suspect was observed to be unable to control himself and acted aggressively. He was subsequently taken to Kajang Hospital and admitted to the psychiatric ward for further treatment,” he said.
He said investigations found that the 26-year-old man was scheduled to board a flight back to Bangladesh at 10.20 pm on the same day.
“The embassy has also been informed of the incident,” he said.
Ravi advised the public against speculating about the incident to prevent the spread of false information that could cause public distress, particularly while at KLIA Terminal 1 and Terminal 2. — Bernama

Title: Missing woman among two found dead in car in Durian Tunggal
Article:
ALOR GAJAH, Sept 20 — A man and a woman were found dead in a car at Taman Inang Sari, Durian Tunggal here around midnight last night.
Alor Gajah district police chief Supt Ahmad Abu Bakar said the bodies of the duo, aged 31 and 33, were discovered at 12.05am.
“A team of personnel dispatched to the scene found that both victims had died, while preliminary checks on the bodies found no elements of foul play, including robbery or signs of a struggle,” he told reporters.
Elaborating, Ahmad said police had earlier received a report on the woman’s disappearance lodged by her mother on September 17 after she could not be located.
He said, however, that police had not had time to take further action on the missing person report before receiving information about the discovery of the two individuals.
“Before the missing person case could be opened, we received information from members of the public about the discovery of the bodies.
“Initial checks found that the woman was the individual reported missing, while the man was believed to be her acquaintance,” he said.
He said based on the condition of the bodies, which had already begun to swell, both victims were believed to have died about three days ago.
“Checks found that both victims were residents of Melaka, with the woman being single. Her employer also informed police that she had not reported for work for the past three days.
The bodies of both victims have been sent to the Forensic Unit for post-mortem examinations to determine the cause of death, and the case has been classified as sudden death. — Bernama

Title: Brother recounts failed attempt to pull mother to safety as grilles trap victims in Tambun fire
Article:
IPOH, Sept 20 — A man described how his younger brother tried to save their mother from a fire early this morning but was unable to pull her out because metal grilles on the balcony blocked the way.
Raja Ikhwan Hadi Raja Ahmad, 47, said his younger brother, Raja Muhammad Shukri, 30, had managed to reach their mother’s hand and tried to pull her to safety, but the grilles prevented him from getting her out of the house.
The fire claimed the lives of their elderly parents, Zaitun Mohamed, 64, and Raja Ahmad Raja Ali, 70, as well as their nephew, Nik Abdurrahman Azimin Harith Helal, 18, in the two-storey terraced house at Persiaran Desa Tambun 4, Taman Desa Tambun here.
Raja Ikhwan Hadi, the eldest of five siblings, said he was asleep near the parking area of his house when he heard his nephew shouting for help, followed by the sound of breaking glass at about 4am.
He said he tried to enter the house but was unable to do so as the fire was already raging and the smoke was thick, while neighbours who came to help also failed to rescue those trapped inside.
An elderly couple and their grandson were killed in a fire involving a two‑storey terraced house at Persiaran Desa Tambun 4, Taman Desa Tambun in Ipoh early this morning. — Bernama pic
“I called for help from the neighbours, who contacted the Fire and Rescue Department and tried to save those inside the house, but they were unsuccessful,” he told reporters at the scene here today.
Raja Ikhwan Hadi said that several hours before the incident, his mother had told him that she had an uneasy feeling, as though something was about to happen.
Meanwhile, Helal Zamri, 37, the father of Nik Abdurrahman Azimin Harith, said he was informed of the incident at about 5.30am and that his son had lived in the house since he was a child and was raised by his maternal grandparents.
“The last time I saw my son and his maternal grandparents was earlier this week, and they were their usual selves, with no sign that anything was amiss. My son worked with me in our catering business,” he said.
Raja Ikhwan Hadi said he had managed to move a motorcycle from the parking area but there was not enough time to save anything else. — Bernama

Title: PM channels RM5,000 initial assistance to Tambun fire victims
Article:
IPOH, Sept 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today contributed RM5,000 in initial assistance to the family of the victims of a fire that claimed the lives of three family members at Persiaran Desa Tambun 4, Taman Desa Tambun, here early this morning.
The contribution was presented by Tambun Member of Parliament’s (MP) special officer Mohamad Hairul Amir Sabri, representing the Tambun MP’s Service Centre, to the family’s representative, Raja Ikhwan Hadi Raja Ahmad.
Mohamad Hairul Amir said the assistance was an initial contribution to ease the burden on the family, which is now coping with the loss of three family members in the tragedy.
“Insya-Allah, tomorrow, the ICU (Implementation Coordination Unit) of the Prime Minister’s Department (JPM) will come to conduct an assessment, and we will try to assist with repairs to the house as well as provide any other assistance needed,” he told reporters at the scene here today.
He said the service centre was also prepared to help provide temporary accommodation if the victim’s family needed a place to stay while the house was being repaired.
“Looking at the condition of the house, the repair process may take quite some time. So, the service centre may help provide temporary accommodation for them until the repairs are completed,” he said.
Mohamad Hairul Amir said they would also discuss with the Social Welfare Department (JKM) and relevant agencies to identify suitable assistance for the victim’s family, including the possibility of providing counselling services.
He said they would also assist with arrangements for the burial of all the victims.
Meanwhile, Mohamad Hairul Amir said the Prime Minister had conveyed his condolences to the victims’ family and instructed the service centre to provide the best possible assistance to the family.
Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) personnel work at the scene after an elderly couple and their grandson were killed in a fire involving a two‑storey terraced house at Persiaran Desa Tambun 4, Taman Desa Tambun in Ipoh September 20, 2026. — Bernama pic
Earlier, an elderly couple and their grandson were killed in a fire involving a two-storey terraced house in the incident early this morning.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director Datuk Sayani Saidon said the department received a call at 4am before a team from the Tambun and Ipoh Fire and Rescue stations rushed to the scene.
The victims were identified as Raja Ahmad Raja Ali, 70, Zaitun Mohamed, 64, and their 18-year-old grandson, Nik Abdurrahman Azimin Harith Helal, while Raja Ikhwan Hadi, 47, survived after he was believed to have been sleeping in the parking area of the house. — Bernama

Title: Technician killed after car skids into opposite lane and hits motorcycle in Dungun
Article:
DUNGUN, Sept 20 — A technician was killed after the motorcycle he was riding was hit by a car that lost control at Kilometre 70 of Jalan Jerangau-Jabor near Bukit Besi here this morning.
Dungun police chief Supt Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat said the 7.30 am incident involved Mohd Yusop Abu Bakar, 34, who worked at a factory in Bukit Besi and was riding a Honda AFS110 motorcycle from Dungun towards Jerangau.
“Initial investigations found that upon reaching the location, a Perodua Myvi driven by a 42-year-old man is believed to have lost control, skidded into the opposite lane and collided with the front of the victim’s motorcycle.
“The motorcyclist suffered serious injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene,” he said in a statement today.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 41 of the Road Transport Act 1987, with further investigations ongoing to determine the actual cause of the accident. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia to follow UN decision on any Malbatt deployment to Yemen, says defence minister
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Sept 20 — Malaysia will be guided by any decision made by the United Nations (UN) should there be a proposal to deploy the Malaysian Battalion (Malbatt) peacekeeping force to Yemen amid the ongoing conflict there, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said.
Mohamed Khaled, who is also Kota Tinggi MP, said Malaysia would not make such a decision unilaterally, stressing that any action must be based on a UN decision.
“Malaysia’s decision will be guided by the decision made by the UN, rather than us acting on our own.
“So it has to be the UN that decides whether to send a peacekeeping force or whatever,” he told reporters after attending the Kota Tinggi parliamentary constituency-level Maulidur Rasul celebration here today.
Mohamed Khaled said peacekeeping forces were normally deployed after parties to a conflict had agreed to a peace settlement, with the forces tasked with ensuring that the terms of the settlement were observed by all parties.
He cited the deployment of peacekeeping forces in Lebanon as an example, saying their role was to ensure that the terms of the peace settlement were respected.
However, he said the situation in Yemen was different as the conflict and fighting were still ongoing.
“The UN has never deployed any force to take part in a war. This is a conflict; a war is still going on,” he said.
He said deploying forces while the war was still ongoing could expose personnel to the risk of losing their lives.
“If you go into the middle of it, there will be casualties and loss of life,” he said.
As such, he said there was no question of Malaysia unilaterally deploying troops to Yemen and that any decision would have to await a UN determination.
The development comes amid a recent escalation in Yemen, with intense fighting along the western coast and the Bab al-Mandab Strait forcing more than 100,000 people to flee their homes. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi: State‑specific political shifts may lead to Pakatan realignments, cooperation with Bersatu not discussed
Article:
KUALA PILAH, Sept 20 — The current political dynamics could lead to various political realignments, taking into account the unique political landscape of each state.
Pakatan Harapan (PH) communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said recent political developments could not be viewed through a single mould, as each state had its own unique political landscape and dynamics.
“We know that each state has its own political uniqueness. So, it is not impossible that such dynamics could also emerge within Pakatan Harapan (PH),” he told reporters here today.
He said this after officiating the Kampung Angkat Madani (Madani Adopted Village) 2025 initiative of the Communications Ministry at Surau Kampung Tebat Kering, Kuala Pilah, here.
Also present were Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah, Kuala Pilah District Council president Nawal Mohamed Amin, Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) deputy editor-in-chief (News Services) Mohd Shukri Ishak, and the ministry’s agencies’ top management.
Commenting on the possibility of cooperation between PH and Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu), Fahmi said there had been no discussions towards such a move so far.
Yesterday, Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said the party would not contest the 16th General Election (GE16) on its own, but as part of a political coalition.
In a separate development, the Communications Minister said the decision to grant a conditional pardon to former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak was subject to Article 42 of the Federal Constitution and fell within the powers of the King.
“On the government’s side, PH itself issued a statement last week. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, who is responsible for representing the government on the Pardons Board, have also issued statements.
“The decision to grant a conditional pardon was made by His Majesty,” he said.
His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, on Friday granted a conditional pardon to Najib, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to him paying a RM50 million fine.
The Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) of the Prime Minister’s Department said the decision was made at the 64th meeting of the Pardons Board for the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya, held at Istana Negara on Friday. — Bernama

Title: Floods: Five relief centres opened in Gua Musang, 221 evacuees housed
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 20 — Five temporary relief centres (PPS) have been opened in Gua Musang following heavy rain since last night, with 221 victims from 57 families housed at the centres as of 1.33pm today.
According to the Social Welfare Department’s (JKM) InfoBencana portal, three districts were affected by the flooding.
The five relief centres are Masjid Jeram Tekoh, Jeram Tekoh Zone 3 Community Hall, Sekolah Kebangsaan Jeram Tekoh, Felda Chiku 6 Community Hall and Sekolah Kebangsaan Limau Kasturi 1.
Meanwhile, Kelantan Civil Defence Force (APM) deputy director Lt Col Mohd Farid Ishak said the Gua Musang district APM had deployed personnel in two main teams to carry out follow-up operations in the affected areas.
He said the post-flood team was tasked with carrying out clean-up operations in Kampung Sungai Asap A and Kampung Renok as floodwaters receded, while the Rescue Team was deployed to assist in evacuating affected residents, particularly in the Limau Kasturi area.
He said Gua Musang APM was also continuing to monitor high-risk areas from time to time and remained on standby to conduct rescue and evacuation operations if necessary.
“Members of the public, particularly those living in low-lying areas and near rivers, are advised to remain vigilant, comply with the authorities’ instructions and immediately move to designated relief centres if instructed,” he said when contacted today. — Bernama

Title: ‘Whether Najib is released or not is a separate issue’: Khaled Nordin says King’s pardon prerogative should not be questioned
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Sept 20 — Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin today said any displeasure over former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s conditional pardon should not extend to questioning the Yang di-Pertuan Agong’s constitutional prerogative to grant them.
Khaled said the granting of pardons was not unprecedented, with such decisions having been made in numerous cases involving individuals sentenced to death or life imprisonment, while the issue should also not be linked to ongoing efforts to unite Malay political parties.
“Pardons have been granted in numerous cases, whether involving individuals sentenced to death or life imprisonment, and those decisions were accepted without dispute,” The New Straits Times quoted him as telling reporters after attending the Kota Tinggi Parliamentary Maulidur Rasul celebration at Dewan Besar Felda Air Tawar 2 here.
“We hope all citizens accept that the power exists and is permissible under the law. It is the absolute prerogative of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong and should not be questioned by any party,” he was quoted as saying.
Khaled, who is also Kota Tinggi MP, said efforts towards Malay political unity were focused on safeguarding the community’s interests and political standing, and had nothing to do with Najib’s pardon.
“Whether Najib is released or not is a separate issue. Malay unity is about safeguarding the community’s interests and political standing. If opponents use the pardon issue to influence voters, it is simply political manoeuvring,” he added.
Khaled also said that his party’s solidarity with Najib fundraiser set up recently is only to provide support within its means.
“It shows our sympathy because RM50 million is a substantial sum. While we may not reach that target, the fund reflects what we can do to help,” he was quoted as saying.
Last Friday, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, granted a conditional pardon allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine.
Umno subsequently launched the solidarity fund to collect public donations, which hit RM1 million as of 9.30am yesterday, according to party secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki.

Title: ‘Lots of noise, then silence’: PAS’ Sanusi questions DAP’s Anthony Loke’s resignation offer over Najib house arrest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — PAS election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor today described the DAP’s decision to have only its secretary-general Anthony Loke offer to resign from the Cabinet over former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s conditional pardon as “firecracker politics”.
Loke offered to resign as Transport Minister yesterday after a three-hour DAP central executive committee meeting, while the party decided its other ministers and deputy ministers would remain in the unity government to maintain political stability.
“Nga said the same thing before. He didn’t resign either. They act as if they’re going to take action, but nothing gets done. It’s firecracker politics. Lots of noise, then silence,” news portal Free Malaysia Today quoted Sanusi as saying.
Sanusi, Kedah menteri besar, was referring to DAP deputy chairman Nga Kor Ming, who had previously said he would resign over Najib’s release but did not ultimately leave the Cabinet.
He also accused DAP of repeatedly changing its position after announcing plans to take stronger action over Najib’s conditional pardon.
“DAP plays flip-flop politics. Next, they’ll find an excuse not to resign. Before this, they said they wanted to leave the government. Then they found an excuse not to,” he was quoted as saying.
Yesterday, Loke said that the DAP respected the Yang di-Pertuan Agong’s constitutional authority to grant pardons but felt the conditional pardon was difficult for Malaysians to accept.
He said his resignation offer was the party’s response to the decision allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to a RM50 million fine.
Najib was granted the conditional pardon last Friday, with the decision allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest while DAP said it would continue supporting Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s unity government.

Title: DAP sec-gen’s Cabinet quit offer over Najib house arrest is his own call, says Umno veep Khaled Nordin
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Sept 20 — Anthony Loke’s offer to resign as Transport Minister following former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s conditional pardon is entirely his own matter, Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said today.
Loke offered to resign yesterday after DAP’s central executive committee meeting, saying the move was the party’s response to the decision allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest, while other DAP ministers would remain in the unity government to maintain political stability.
“From Umno’s perspective, that is his matter. Whether he wants to resign or not, that is his matter,”
The Star
quoted Khaled as replying to reporters after attending a Maulidur Rasul celebration at Felda Air Tawar 2 here.
Khaled, who is also defence minister, said Loke’s resignation offer should not be confused with the decision involving Najib.
Khaled reiterated that the decision to grant Najib a conditional pardon and allow him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest was within the constitutional prerogative of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
He said Umno welcomed the decision and would respect the authority exercised by the King.
Loke said yesterday that DAP respected the Yang di-Pertuan Agong’s power to grant pardons but had its own position on Najib’s conditional pardon, which he said was difficult for the party to accept.
He said only he would offer to resign, while the other DAP ministers and deputy ministers would remain in government to ensure political stability.
Najib was granted a conditional pardon last Friday allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine.
He has been serving a six-year prison sentence at Kajang Prison since August 2022 after the Federal Court upheld his conviction and 12-year jail term for misappropriating RM42 million from SRC International, with the sentence and fine later reduced by the Pardons Board in 2024.

Title: Sentul OCPD: Police to deploy mobile station near Najib’s Langgak Duta residence from tomorrow; Prisons Dept to handle monitoring
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — A mobile police station will be deployed near a former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s official residence in Langgak Duta here from tomorrow to facilitate security arrangements during any transfer from prison to the residence.
Sentul district police chief ACP Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said the mobile police station was scheduled to be deployed at the residence from 7am tomorrow.
“The mobile police station is not for the purpose of providing 24-hour security for Datuk Seri Najib. It is to provide security during his return process, including for local and foreign media, neighbours, and to prevent traffic congestion and the presence of supporters,” he said when contacted today.
On the status of the residence as the location for the house arrest, Anuar Bakri said police had yet to receive any official confirmation.
“I cannot confirm it because I have not received any information either, but one of Datuk Seri Najib’s official residences is under my jurisdiction. There is a possibility that other residences belonging to him are also being considered,” he said.
On the agency responsible for monitoring Najib if he serves his sentence under house arrest, Anuar Bakri said based on information received, the responsibility would lie with the Malaysian Prisons Department and not the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM).
According to him, four Prisons Department officers had visited the residence yesterday to conduct an inspection and assessment.
“The responsibility is under the Prisons Department because four prison officers came yesterday to conduct an inspection and assessment. PDRM will only facilitate Datuk Seri Najib’s movement and, at the same time, ensure the safety of the media,” he said.
He added that the police deployment during the process was expected to comprise one supervisor and two personnel, supported by a mobile patrol vehicle (MPV) unit.
Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar was reported yesterday as saying that the standard operating procedures for Najib’s house arrest would cover matters including visits, security and monitoring of the former prime minister’s movements after the relevant official letter was received.
On Friday, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, consented to a conditional pardon allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine.
The Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister’s Department said the order was decided at the 64th meeting of the Pardons Board for the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya, held at Istana Negara.
Najib has been serving his prison sentence at Kajang Prison since August 23, 2022, following his conviction in the SRC International case. — Bernama

Title: MEF: RM1,000 Socso mobility allowance to improve job matching for workers relocating over 100km
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — The one-off RM1,000 Mobility Assistance Allowance for eligible Social Security Organisation (Socso) contributors is expected to improve the matching of workers with job opportunities, particularly where vacancies are located beyond their immediate areas.
Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) Senior Adviser for Government, Media and International Engagement Datuk Dr Syed Hussain Syed Husman said the initiative recognised that relocation and extended travel could involve significant upfront costs for workers to take jobs farther from home.
“From employers’ perspective, improving geographical mobility will contribute to a more efficient labour market by enabling vacancies to be matched with suitable workers beyond the immediate local area.
“This is particularly relevant in sectors and regions where employers continue to face difficulties in sourcing workers with the required skills and experience,” he said in a statement today.
However, Syed Hussain said MEF encouraged Socso to clearly communicate the eligibility criteria, application procedures and payment timelines to workers and employers.
Yesterday, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan announced that the government would provide a one-off RM1,000 Mobility Assistance Allowance to Socso contributors who secure new jobs located more than 100 kilometres from their homes.
He said the allowance would take effect on Oct 1 through amendments to the Employment Insurance System (EIS) Act 2017.
On the broader enhancements to the EIS, Syed Hussain said the increase in the Early Re-employment Allowance from 25 per cent to 50 per cent of the remaining unpaid Job Search Allowance would provide additional support for eligible workers who return to employment early.
He said the increase in the daily Training Allowance from RM10 to RM30, together with the increase in the maximum training fee covered from RM4,000 to RM7,000, would further strengthen the EIS in helping unemployed workers reskill and transition into new employment.
Syed Hussain said employers could also benefit from employment services and worker-support programmes that help reduce the time taken to fill vacancies and improve the matching of suitable candidates with available jobs. — Bernama

Title: Prisons Dept says still waiting for official notice before Najib’s house arrest can start
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s move from prison to house arrest has yet to get the formal green light from the Malaysian Prisons Department, which says it is still waiting for official written notification of the conditional pardon granted to the former prime minister.
The Federal Territories Pardons Board granted Najib a conditional pardon on Friday, allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to conditions including payment of a RM50 million fine.
“In this regard, in line with the statement by Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution smail, Minister of Home Affairs on September 19, 2026, the Home Ministry and Malaysian Prisons Department are still awaiting official written notification regarding the decision before any further action to implement the decision can be determined.
“Any notification and official documents relating to the Pardons Board’s decision will be conveyed through the appropriate official channels before being submitted to the Malaysian Prisons Department for further action,” the department said in a statement today.
The department said it was ready to carry out any official instructions received from the relevant authorities in accordance with the law, prison regulations and procedures currently in force.
It also said any decision or instruction received would be carried out in an orderly, professional and transparent manner.
The department urged all parties to refer to official sources and refrain from speculating about how the decision would be implemented.
Najib, who has been held at Kajang Prison since August 2022, is serving a six-year sentence after the Federal Territory Pardons Board in 2024 reduced his original 12-year jail term and RM210 million fine for the SRC International case to six years and RM50 million.
The conditional royal pardon allows him to serve the remainder of that sentence under house arrest, but the RM50 million fine remains among the conditions attached to the decision.

Title: Education Ministry to revisit 2006 tuition centre ownership provisions, proposal goes to Cabinet next week
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 20 — The Education Ministry (MOE) will submit a proposal to review the ownership structure of tuition centres for Cabinet consideration next week.
In a statement today, MOE said the provisions on tuition centre ownership were detailed in the Private Educational Institutions Policy Book published in 2006.
“MOE takes note of the various views raised regarding the provisions and is always open to hearing the views of all parties.
“MOE believes that the education sector should remain open to all parties who wish to contribute to the development and learning of children in Malaysia,” it said.
The ministry also said it appreciated the contributions of tuition centre operators over the years and would continue to work with all parties in the interest of children’s education in Malaysia. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak agrees in principle to RM1.5b allocation for Sibu Economic Zone, deputy premier says
Article:
SIBU, Sept 20 — The Sarawak government has agreed in principle to an initial RM1.5 billion allocation to establish the Sibu Economic Zone (SEZ) as a dedicated platform to coordinate and shape the city’s economic development.
Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Dr Sim Kui Hian said the SEZ would focus on investment, the service sector and high-value employment.
“Sibu’s development will also be supported by stronger connectivity and industrial capacity, including the proposed West Bank Bridge and the Sibu Industrial Park, which is scheduled for completion in 2029.
“The proposed Bukit Assek redevelopment, which has received in-principle approval, is another important long-term initiative aimed at moving Sibu towards a more sustainable and higher-value economic direction,” he said at the Association of Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry of Sarawak (ACCCIS) annual general meeting here.
Also present was ACCCIS president Kong Chiong Ung.
Dr Sim said ACCCIS and its affiliated chambers had over the years provided an important platform for business networking, policy dialogue, capacity building and engagement between the government and business community.
The State Public health, Housing and Local Government Minister said the business community had an important role in Sarawak’s development, adding that the government valued the contribution of chambers such as ACCCIS in conveying businesses’ views and concerns.
“I encourage ACCCIS to continue serving as a constructive bridge between the government and the business community, particularly in identifying practical issues affecting businesses and contributing ideas towards Sarawak’s economic development,” he said.
Dr Sim said the private sector had an important role in turning policies, infrastructure and development platforms into actual investment, business activity and employment.
“Government development alone cannot achieve the full potential of Sibu or Sarawak. This is why organisations such as ACCCIS remain important partners to the government.”
He said the government would continue providing policy direction, infrastructure and platforms for growth, while businesses must be prepared to invest, innovate and identify new opportunities.
He also encouraged ACCCIS to continue bringing together businesses from across Sarawak and strengthening cooperation among its affiliated chambers.
“Through closer government-business collaboration, we can build a stronger, more resilient and more competitive Sarawak economy.”
D Sim also commended ACCCIS for extending its contribution beyond business advocacy, particularly through initiatives promoting environmental awareness, resource recycling and sustainable living.
He said the ‘How to Retain the Blue Sky Eco-Enzyme Public Workshop’ in 2024 and ‘How to Retain the Blue Sky 2.0: Five Eco Enzyme Lessons’ in 2026 demonstrated ACCCIS’ continued commitment to environmental sustainability.
He said the second workshop in June also saw eco-enzyme initiatives extended to schools to encourage environmental awareness among students.
“These initiatives are aligned with Sarawak’s Post Covid-19 Development Strategy 2030, which places economic prosperity, social inclusivity and environmental sustainability as the three key dimensions of Sarawak’s development vision.”
Dr Sim said environmental protection was not only an ecological responsibility but was increasingly connected to the future economy, including green industries, renewable energy and new high-value opportunities.
Looking forward, he said Sarawak was entering an important phase of economic transformation and must continue moving beyond traditional industries while developing new economic sectors, knowledge and technical capabilities.
He identified renewable and green energy, semiconductors, healthcare, digitalisation and technology-related industries as key areas for future growth.
Dr Sim also commended ACCCIS for launching its Digital Membership Database Management System yesterday.
“This is a positive step that shows ACCCIS is embracing digitalisation and moving in the same direction as Sarawak’s broader transformation towards a more digital and technology-driven economy,” he said. — The Borneo Post

Title: No one should feel obliged to help pay RM50m fine, Najib tells supporters as Umno solidarity fund hits RM1m
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak says Malaysians who have offered to help pay the RM50 million fine required under his conditional royal pardon should not feel “burdened or obliged” to do so.
The statement from his lawyers comes as the Najib Razak Solidarity Fund set up by Umno to help him meet the payment reached RM1 million by 9.30am yesterday, less than a day after it was launched.
“While our client is deeply touched by these expressions of solidarity, he does not wish the Party, its members and supporters, or members of the public to feel burdened or obliged on his account,” Najib’s lawyers in the firm Messrs Shafee & Co said in a statement issued on his behalf.
The lawyers said Najib was grateful to those who had offered assistance towards meeting the condition imposed under his conditional pardon, but stressed that such support should be given “entirely of their own free will and according to their respective means”.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the fund collected RM165,645 within its first hour and RM634,562.02 within three hours, with many contributors giving RM10 or RM50.
Asyraf later announced that the fund had reached RM1 million and urged supporters to continue contributing, including donations of RM10.
The fund was launched after Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said contributions were open to party leaders, members and supporters, as well as anyone wishing to show their support voluntarily.
Zahid also said the initiative would be carried out transparently and systematically while complying with all applicable regulations and laws.
The fundraising effort has drawn mixed reactions online, with some questioning the decision to raise money for Najib and whether such funds could instead help people facing financial hardship.
The Federal Territories Pardons Board granted Najib a conditional pardon on Friday, allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine and other conditions.
The Attorney General has clarified that the conditional pardon applies only to the prison sentence imposed in the SRC International case.

Title: Saifuddin Nasution: Proposed House Arrest Act focuses on remand detainees and prison overcrowding
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — The proposed House Arrest Act is aimed at addressing prison overcrowding, particularly involving remand detainees, who make up a significant proportion of the prison population while awaiting trial.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail stressed that the proposal was not new, saying he had mooted it as one of the Home Ministry’s (KDN) measures since 2024 to reduce prison overcrowding and ensure the country’s correctional system is managed more effectively.
“The concept we have been discussing from the outset is clear, namely that for remand detainees who meet the requirements, the court may consider placing them under house arrest with electronic monitoring until their trial.
“Serious criminal cases have already been identified for exclusion from this mechanism.
“We do not yet have an act or law on house arrest. Previously, I mooted introducing one specifically for remand detainees, as remand detainees are one of the causes of prison overcrowding,” he said in a video uploaded on his Facebook page today.
Saifuddin Nasution said prison inmates comprised those who had been convicted and were serving their sentences, as well as remand detainees whose court proceedings had yet to be completed.
He said remand detainees referred to individuals who had been charged but were either denied bail or unable to post bail, resulting in them being held in prison pending trial.
“So, this combination of convicted inmates and remand detainees contributes to prison overcrowding. For example, we currently have 41 prisons, but the prison population is 93,000. Our prison capacity is 75,000,” he said.
He said if the proposed law was passed, the court could consider placing eligible remand detainees under house arrest, with their movements monitored using electronic devices until their trial date.
Saifuddin Nasution said the Cabinet had also given in-principle approval for KDN to begin the process of drafting and tabling the House Arrest Act in Parliament.
“The original objective remains the same, namely to reduce prison overcrowding and ensure that the country’s correctional system can be managed more effectively. That is the original context and purpose of the House Arrest Act that we have been discussing from the outset.
“If the Bill is passed, we can release these remand detainees to their homes and equip them with modern devices to monitor their movements until their trial date. That is the original purpose we have been discussing,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Frozen assets may hinder RM50m payment for Najib’s house arrest, his lawyers say
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s ability to pay the RM50 million fine required for his house arrest could be complicated by frozen assets, bank accounts and properties subject to government enforcement proceedings, according to his lawyers.
The legal firm Messrs Shafee & Co said a “significant part” of Najib’s assets remained subject to freezing orders and enforcement proceedings, meaning their disposal was not presently within his sole control.
“His ability to satisfy the condition therefore turns in part on matters that do not lie in his own hands,” the lawyers said in a statement issued on Najib’s behalf.
Najib remains at Kajang Prison in the meantime and will only be transferred to house arrest once the conditions are satisfied, the lawyers added.
Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said yesterday that Najib must first pay the RM50 million fine at the Kuala Lumpur High Court Registrar’s Office before the house-arrest process can proceed.
The Federal Territories Pardons Board granted Najib a conditional pardon on Friday, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to the payment and other conditions.
Najib’s lawyers also thanked the King and the Federal Territories Pardons Board for the decision, while Najib expressed gratitude to Deputy Prime Minister and Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, the Umno supreme council and the party and Barisan Nasional leadership and members for their support.
Najib has been serving a six-year sentence at Kajang Prison since August 2022 after the Federal Court upheld his conviction in the SRC International case; his original 12-year sentence and RM210 million fine were reduced to six years and RM50 million respectively following a 2024 pardon.

Title: Perak Fire Dept: Tambun house blaze leaves three family members dead, one injured
Article:
IPOH, Sept 20 — An elderly couple and their grandson were killed in a fire involving a two-storey terraced house at Persiaran Desa Tambun 4, Taman Desa Tambun here early this morning.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director Datuk Sayani Saidon said the department received a call at 4 am before a team from the Tambun and Ipoh Fire and Rescue Stations rushed to the scene.
She said the victims were identified as Raja Ahmad Raja Ali, 70, Zaitun Mohamed, 64, and Nik Abdurrahman Azimin Harith Helal, 18, while another victim, Raja Ikhwan Hadi Raja Ahmad, 47, survived after he was believed to have been sleeping in the house’s parking area.
“Upon arrival at the scene, the fire and rescue vehicles found that a Class A two-storey terraced house measuring 20 by 70 feet was on fire, with about 70 per cent of the house affected,” she said in a statement today.
Sayani said the 70-year-old male victim was found in the bathroom on the ground floor of the house, while the other two victims were found on the upper floor.
“One victim was found in the upstairs bathroom while another was found in a bedroom near a window on the upper floor of the house,” she said.
Based on the information received, all the victims were related, and six people lived in the house, but only four people were inside the house when the incident occurred.
She said the fire had been completely extinguished and the operation ended at 8 am today, with all the victims handed over to the police for further action. — Bernama

Title: Haze: Sarawak areas dominate unhealthy API readings, IPD Serian highest at 182
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — Twenty-two areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 9am today.
According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, the highest reading was recorded at IPD Serian (182) in Sarawak, while seven areas in the state also recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Samarahan (168), Kuching (166), Sri Aman (163), Bintulu (153), Sibu (152), Sarikei (116) and Samalaju (105).
Five areas in Johor also recorded unhealthy API readings, with Larkin recording 162, Batu Pahat and Pasir Gudang 155 each, followed by Segamat (154) and Tangkak (153).
Meanwhile, Putrajaya and Nilai (Negeri Sembilan) each recorded a reading of 154, while Shah Alam, Selangor recorded 152, followed by Cheras, Kuala Lumpur (133) and Seremban, Negeri Sembilan (127).
Unhealthy API readings were also recorded at Bukit Rambai, Melaka (121), Bandaraya Melaka (114), Johan Setia, Selangor (112) and Petaling Jaya, Selangor (102).
Meanwhile, 40 areas recorded moderate readings, while five areas recorded good readings.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 (moderate), 101 to 200 (unhealthy), 201 to 300 (very unhealthy) and 301 and above (hazardous).
Meanwhile, Department of Environment (DOE) deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon, in a statement today, said that the situation was occurring amid persistent dry weather conditions in parts of the southern Asean region.
Based on a report by the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) yesterday (Sept 19), 865 hotspots were detected in Kalimantan, 16 in Sumatra and six in Malaysia, all in Sarawak.
The ASMC also reported moderate to dense smoke plumes from clusters of hotspots in several areas in Kalimantan and southern Sumatra, with moderate transboundary smoke plumes from Kalimantan moving towards western Sarawak and southern Sabah.
She said haze from southern Sumatra and Kalimantan was also observed moving towards Singapore and southern Peninsular Malaysia.
Meanwhile, DOE said it continued to monitor the risk of fires, particularly in peatland areas and landfill sites that are vulnerable to fires during hot and dry weather.
DOE said monitoring would be stepped up if there was an increase in air pollution, while appropriate action would be taken in accordance with its jurisdiction and legal provisions to minimise the impact on the environment and public health.
“Enforcement action has also been strengthened through inspections and patrols in identified high-risk areas, including agricultural areas, peatlands, plantations, landfill sites and locations with potential for open burning,” the statement said.
DOE also monitors API readings, hotspots and developments in transboundary haze, taking into account meteorological information to assess the situation and coordinate haze management measures at district, state and national levels.
Under the National Haze Action Plan (PTJK), the Disaster Management Committee can be activated by NADMA when the API reading exceeds 150 for more than 24 hours.
The PTJK also stipulates the suspension of outdoor activities when the API reading exceeds 100, the closure of schools, kindergartens and childcare centres when the API reading exceeds 200, while cloud seeding operations may be carried out, subject to the presence of clouds and suitable weather conditions, when the API reading exceeds 150 for more than 24 hours.
The department also urged the public not to carry out open burning, particularly during hot and dry weather and when air quality is at unhealthy to hazardous levels.
It added that under the Environmental Quality (Amendment) Act 2024, offences involving open burning are punishable by a minimum fine of RM25,000 up to RM1 million, or imprisonment for up to five years, or both, while a compound of up to 50 per cent of the maximum fine may also be imposed for each offence.
The public is also urged to report fires or incidents of open burning to the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department via the 999 emergency line or DOE’s toll-free line at 1-800-88-2727.
“Hourly API readings can be accessed via DOE’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) or the official MyJAS EQMS application,” it said. — Bernama

Title: Fire razes 10‑door longhouse in remote Penan settlement in Ulu Baram
Article:
MIRI, Sept 20 — A 10-door longhouse in Kampung Long Jekitan, Ulu Baram, Marudi was completely destroyed in a fire yesterday.
The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) operation control centre said a distress call was received at about 2.50pm, following which the Marudi Police Station was immediately alerted.
It said initial information received indicated that the 10-door longhouse, which was a non-permanent structure, was completely destroyed by fire.
“As the incident location is relatively remote and is estimated to take about eight hours to reach via logging roads, the dispatched team from Marudi fire station would proceed to the location the following day, on September 20,” the department said.
Long Jekitan is a remote Penan Silat settlement located along Sungai Silat in the interior of Upper Baram, near the Indonesian border and east of the Usun Apau plateau. — The Borneo Post

Title: Rescued Croatian hiker fined RM25,000 over Mount Kinabalu climb says trespassing was ‘last thing on my mind’
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 20 — Croatian hiker Mauro Persic, who was fined RM25,000 for trespassing into Kinabalu Park, has denied deliberately entering the mountain without permission or trying to avoid paying the entry fee.
The 46-year-old, who lives in London, said his climb was spontaneous and driven by his desire to explore Mount Kinabalu after seeing its beauty firsthand.
“I did not want to trespass nor avoid paying entry fees, that was the last thing on my mind. All I wanted to do was explore the captivating beauty of Kinabalu the moment I saw it,” he said in a Facebook post a day after Malaysia Day.
“As I have done many times before in different places around the globe. I did it on a spur of a moment and did not put enough thought and consideration to it. My sincere apologies for this.”
Persic also apologised to Sabahans who felt he had disrespected them, saying he had no intention of offending the state’s people, culture or the mountain.
“I would like to make an apology to all the people of Sabah who feel that I have disrespected them. I never meant any disrespect to people, culture nor mountain,” he said.
“People of Sabah have treated me like one of their own and I have only words of praise for them.”
Persic said he had also tried to respect the environment during the climb, claiming he left no trace behind and avoided climbing major peaks because of their sacred significance to the Kadazan-Dusun community.
“However, I have been as respectful as ever to the environment, leaving no trace behind and not climbing on top of any major peaks out of respect for sacred meaning that the mountain holds for Kadazan-Dusun people,” he said.
He said he did not consider his climb a conquest of Mount Kinabalu, questioning the idea of “conquering” mountains.
“Lastly, I did not conquer Kinabalu (nor any other mountain for that matter) and I find this commonly quoted concept wrong on so many levels,” he said.
“We might spend a fleeting moment on a peak but the mountain will remain there long after we're gone. Besides, why would one need to conquer anyways?”
Persic’s unauthorised climb came to light on Sept 6 after he sent an SOS when he was injured and stranded on a ledge along a steep slope.
A five-day rescue operation involving 43 personnel eventually brought him to safety, with a porter carrying him down the mountain after rescuers faced steep terrain, rain and poor visibility.
Persic sustained injuries to his right leg and ribs, as well as minor wounds to his hands.
He ended his post with a message for Malaysians: “I wish Happy Malaysia Day to all Malaysians, wherever they might be!”
